intro.title: Egg white to aquafaba conversion: liquid or powder
intro.description: Convert egg whites to liquid or powdered aquafaba with clear weights, a five-white meringue example, and practical storage and format guidance for bakers.
intro.h1: How to convert egg whites to aquafaba, liquid or powder
intro.texto: Your meringue recipe calls for five egg whites; use 150g of liquid VERY AQUAFABA, or 10g of powder with 150 ml of water. Use 30g of liquid VERY AQUAFABA for each egg white. When you are scaling trays of meringues or revising a production formula, start from what the recipe gives you: an egg-white count or an egg-white weight. Enter either one in the converter. It returns the liquid aquafaba weight, the powder weight, the water to add and the weight after making up the powder. A five-white recipe and a recipe written as 150g of egg white start at the same point. Use liquid when you want aquafaba ready to weigh, or make up powder only for the batch in front of you. For whole eggs and yolks, convert the egg component separately before you adjust the rest of the formula.

secciones.h2: Start with what your recipe tells you
secciones.texto:
Read the ingredient line before you change any method. A formula that lists five egg whites and one that lists 150g of egg white both lead to the same starting conversion. Enter the count when the recipe uses eggs. Enter the weight when the recipe has already been written for a scale.

The converter returns four working figures: liquid aquafaba in grams, powder in grams, water in ml and the weight once the powder is made up. Keep the egg-white quantity separate from whole egg or yolk ingredients. Whole eggs use a different conversion, and yolks need aquafaba plus oil where their richness matters. Use the whole egg converter or recipe converter for those lines rather than folding them into your egg-white number.

secciones.h2: See what five egg whites become
secciones.texto:
Five egg whites convert to 150g of liquid VERY AQUAFABA. With powder, make up 10g of powder with 150 ml of water first. That prepared quantity weighs 160g, so make it up, then weigh the amount your formula calls for. Do not add the powder dry to the mix.

For five egg whites in meringue:

IngredientQuantity
Liquid VERY AQUAFABA150g
VERY AQUAFABA powder10g
Water for the powder150 ml
Sugar150g

For the meringue method, chill the aquafaba to 4 °C, whip for 3 to 5 minutes, then bake at 90 °C for 1.5 to 2 hours. This quantity makes about 30 meringues.

secciones.h2: Weigh your aquafaba before you start
secciones.texto:
Put the bowl on the scale and weigh the aquafaba that goes into the recipe. A formula written for 150g of egg white takes 150g of liquid VERY AQUAFABA. When you use powder for that same conversion, make up 10g of powder with 150 ml of water before you weigh the prepared aquafaba.

The powder and water figures are not interchangeable with the liquid figure. The powder route gives you 160g once made up, while the liquid route gives you 150g to add. Making the powder separately lets you prepare what the batch needs, then keep the rest of the formula unchanged unless the recipe itself calls for another adjustment.

secciones.h2: Use the converted quantity in your recipe
secciones.texto:
Choose liquid when you want ready-made aquafaba available to weigh across several bakes. A 1L Tetrapak replaces 33 egg whites, while a 10L bag-in-box replaces 330. For smaller or changing batches, powder lets you make up only the quantity you need. A 30g pouch replaces 15 egg whites.

Unopened liquid and powder keep for at least 12 months at room temperature. Once opened, keep liquid at 2 to 6 °C for 3 to 4 days and mark the opening date. Keep opened powder dry and closed until the best-before date on the pouch. Check the conversion before you set out the rest of your mise en place.

faq.question: How do I convert five egg whites to aquafaba?
faq.answer: Use 150g of liquid VERY AQUAFABA. If you use powder, make up 10g of powder with 150 ml of water before using it in the recipe.

faq.question: How do I convert 150g of egg white to aquafaba?
faq.answer: Use 150g of liquid VERY AQUAFABA. The powder conversion is 10g of powder with 150 ml of water, which makes 160g once prepared.

faq.question: Can I add aquafaba powder straight into my pastry mix?
faq.answer: No. Make up the powder with water first, then weigh the prepared aquafaba for the recipe. Make up only the quantity needed for the batch.

faq.question: How do I convert whole eggs and yolks instead of egg whites?
faq.answer: One whole egg converts to 45g of aquafaba. One yolk converts to 15g of aquafaba plus 10g of oil where the recipe needs the yolk's richness.

faq.question: How do I use aquafaba for a meringue recipe?
faq.answer: Use 150g of aquafaba and 150g of sugar for a five-egg-white meringue formula. Chill the aquafaba to 4 °C, whip for 3 to 5 minutes, then bake at 90 °C for 1.5 to 2 hours.

faq.question: How do I store opened liquid or powder aquafaba?
faq.answer: Keep opened liquid aquafaba at 2 to 6 °C and use it within 3 to 4 days. Keep opened powder dry and closed, then use it by the best-before date on the pouch.

end.cierre: Enter the egg-white count or weight from your recipe, then write down the liquid or powder and water result beside your mise en place. For a meringue batch, chill the measured aquafaba before whipping. If the recipe calls for whole eggs or yolks, use the separate converter before you scale the rest of the formula.

intro.title: How much aquafaba equals one egg?
intro.description: Convert whole eggs to liquid or powdered aquafaba. Get the 45g rule, a 1 to 6 egg table, liquid adjustments, and mixing steps for cakes and batters too.
intro.h1: How much aquafaba equals one egg?
intro.texto:
As you scale a cake batter, one whole egg equals 45g of liquid VERY AQUAFABA, or 3g of powder made up with 45 ml of water. Keep the replacement in grams, not spoons.

That rule gives you a starting weight for cakes, batters and doughs that call for whole eggs. Count the eggs, weigh the aquafaba, then check the recipe’s other liquids before you mix. Whole eggs bring less water than aquafaba, so a small adjustment to milk or another liquid may be needed. The table below converts 1 to 6 whole eggs, and the chocolate cake example shows how to put the number into a real batter. If your recipe separates yolks from whites, treat the yolks as their own ingredient rather than applying the whole-egg rule to everything.

secciones.h2: Convert the whole eggs in your recipe
secciones.texto:
Count only the whole eggs named in the ingredient list. Multiply the count by 45 for liquid aquafaba, or by 3 for powder. Make powder up with the matching water amount before it reaches the bowl. The converter uses grams because aquafaba is weighed. Do not change to tablespoons or cups when scaling a cake, batter or dough.

Start with the ingredient list rather than an egg size on the carton, then use the same result throughout the recipe. That keeps the replacement clear when the batch grows.

secciones.h2: Four eggs in a chocolate cake
secciones.texto:
A chocolate cake with four whole eggs needs 180g of liquid aquafaba. If you are using powder, make up 12g with 180 ml of water before mixing it into the batter. This is a whole-egg conversion, so keep the recipe’s other egg ingredients separate if it names them.

Check the milk or other liquids next, because liquid aquafaba adds more water than the eggs it replaces. Once those amounts are set, follow the cake method rather than treating the aquafaba as a last-minute add-in. Weigh the amount for the batch before you begin creaming, whisking or folding.

secciones.h2: What about the yolk? And why adjust the liquids?
secciones.texto:
Use the whole-egg conversion only where the ingredient list says whole eggs. When yolks are listed on their own and their richness matters, use 15g of aquafaba plus 10g of oil for each yolk. Do not add that oil to a recipe that calls only for whole eggs.

Aquafaba is 90 to 95% water, while a whole egg is about 75% water. Start by reducing the recipe’s other liquids by 5 to 10%. For 200 ml of milk, start with 180 to 190 ml. Water used to make up powder stays at the stated amount.

secciones.h2: Weigh it, then follow your recipe's method
secciones.texto:
Set the scale beside the bowl and weigh the replacement before you start the method. For a fat-rich batter, mix the aquafaba with the sugar before it meets the fat. If the recipe is built around whipped egg whites, chill the aquafaba to 4 to 6 °C, whip it, then fold it in as the method directs.

Make powder up with water first, never add it dry. Prepare only the amount the batch needs. Keep the water used for powder in place, and make the liquid adjustment only to the recipe’s other liquids.

faq.question: How much liquid aquafaba do I use if I replace one whole egg?
faq.answer: Use 45g of liquid VERY AQUAFABA for one whole egg. Weigh it on a scale before adding it to your cake, batter or dough.

faq.question: How do I replace one whole egg with powder if I am baking?
faq.answer: Make up 3g of powder with 45 ml of water for each whole egg. Mix the powder with water first, then add the prepared aquafaba to the recipe.

faq.question: Can I use tablespoons if I am replacing a whole egg?
faq.answer: Weigh 45g of aquafaba per whole egg rather than counting tablespoons. The converter uses grams so you can keep the replacement consistent across batch sizes.

faq.question: How do I convert four whole eggs in my chocolate cake?
faq.answer: Use 180g of liquid aquafaba for four whole eggs. With powder, use 12g of powder made up with 180 ml of water.

faq.question: Should I reduce the milk if I use aquafaba for whole eggs?
faq.answer: Start by reducing the recipe’s other liquids by 5 to 10% when replacing whole eggs. If the recipe uses 200 ml of milk, start with 180 to 190 ml, while keeping powder reconstitution water as stated.

faq.question: What do I do if my recipe lists yolks separately?
faq.answer: For each yolk listed separately, use 15g of aquafaba plus 10g of oil where the yolk’s richness is needed. Keep that conversion separate from any whole eggs in the same recipe.

end.cierre: Count the whole eggs in your next recipe, choose liquid or powder, and weigh the matching amount before you begin mixing. For powder, make it up with water first. If you need stock for a batch, use buy VERY AQUAFABA to choose the format that matches how you work.

intro.title: Aquafaba powder calculator for bakery batches
intro.description: Calculate aquafaba powder for bakery batches: convert egg whites into powder, water and made-up aquafaba, then choose a pouch that covers the full order.
intro.h1: Aquafaba powder calculator: powder and water per egg white
intro.texto: A meringue order is on the bench and calls for 20 egg whites. To replace 20 egg whites, weigh 40g of VERY AQUAFABA powder and make it up with 600 ml of water: 640g of aquafaba. That is the batch check before you mix sugar, set the mixer, or plan a larger production run. Enter the number of egg whites you need, or the made-up aquafaba weight in grams or kilos, and work from the powder and water amounts. The calculator also shows which pouch covers the batch, so you can select a format without making up more than the order calls for. For meringue, make up the powder first and chill the aquafaba before whipping. If the order changes, recalculate the quantity, weigh the powder, and add only the water needed for that batch.

secciones.h2: Calculate the powder and water for your batch
secciones.texto:
Enter the egg white count when your production sheet is written in egg whites. You can also start with the made-up aquafaba weight in grams or kilos. The calculator returns powder in grams, water in ml, and made-up aquafaba weight for the batch. Use the egg white converter if the order records its egg white quantity another way. secciones.texto:
The 20-egg-white batch gives you 640g of made-up aquafaba. A 30g pouch holds enough powder for 15 egg whites, so use a 200g pouch for this amount without making up the full pouch.

For aquafaba meringue, 150g of aquafaba and 150g of sugar make about 30 meringues. Chill the aquafaba to 4 °C, whip for 3 to 5 minutes, then bake at 90 °C for 1.5 to 2 hours.

Measure the made-up aquafaba for the recipe you are producing. Keep the remaining powder dry and closed for a later batch.

secciones.h2: How much aquafaba does each pouch make?
secciones.texto:
Pouch capacity helps you choose your aquafaba powder format before you weigh the batch. The figures below show what each pouch holds, not an instruction to make it up at once. secciones.h2: Weigh the powder, then make up only what you need
secciones.texto:
Set a clean container on the scale and weigh the powder before adding water. Powder is made up with water first, never added dry to the mix. When the production sheet calls for 1kg of made-up aquafaba, use 62.5g of powder and 937.5 ml of water.

For the batch in hand, make up the powder only in the quantity you need. Then chill the made-up aquafaba as you would liquid aquafaba. For meringue, chill it to 4 °C before whipping.

Keep an opened pouch dry and closed until its best-before date. This lets you prepare a smaller batch when the order does not need the full pouch.

faq.question: How do I calculate powder and water for one egg white?
faq.answer: Use 2g of powder and 30 ml of water for one egg white. This makes 32g of aquafaba, the same as 32g of liquid aquafaba.

faq.question: Can I use a 30g pouch for 20 egg whites?
faq.answer: No. Twenty egg whites need 40g of powder and 600 ml of water. A 30g pouch covers 15 egg whites, while a 200g pouch covers the 20-egg-white batch.

faq.question: How do I make up 1kg of aquafaba?
faq.answer: For 1kg of made-up aquafaba, weigh 62.5g of powder and add 937.5 ml of water. Use this quantity when your bakery production sheet is written by weight rather than egg whites.

faq.question: Can I add powder straight to my meringue mix?
faq.answer: No. Make up the powder with water first, then use the made-up aquafaba in the recipe. For meringue, chill the made-up aquafaba to 4 °C before whipping.

faq.question: How do I keep made-up aquafaba cold for meringue?
faq.answer: Chill it to 4 °C before whipping. The meringue method uses 150g of aquafaba with 150g of sugar, then whips the mixture for 3 to 5 minutes.

faq.question: How do I store an opened pouch of aquafaba powder?
faq.answer: Keep an opened pouch dry and closed until the best-before date printed on the pouch. Unopened powder keeps for at least 12 months at room temperature.

end.cierre: Start with the egg white count for the order, then weigh the powder and water for that amount. Check pouch capacity before you open it. When you need a format for your next bakery batch, you can buy VERY AQUAFABA in the pouch size that matches the quantity you make up.

intro.title: Egg replacement calculator for recipe conversion
intro.description: Use this egg replacement calculator to convert whole eggs, extra whites and yolks to liquid or powder aquafaba, including oil and liquid adjustments needed.
intro.h1: How do I use an egg replacement calculator?
intro.texto: At the bench, enter 3 whole eggs, 2 extra whites and 1 extra yolk in the egg replacement calculator. It returns 210g of liquid aquafaba plus 10g of oil, or 14g of powder made up with 210 ml of water plus 10g of oil. Use 45g of liquid aquafaba for each whole egg. Keep whole eggs, separate whites and separate yolks in their own fields. That keeps a yolk already inside a whole egg from being counted twice. The calculator also separates the oil needed where yolk richness matters from the aquafaba used for whipping. If your formula includes whole eggs, adjust its other liquids after you convert them. If it only uses extra whites, leave those liquids as they are. Choose liquid for direct measuring, or make up powder with water before it reaches the bowl.

secciones.h2: Enter your whole eggs, extra whites and yolks
secciones.texto:
Start with the egg quantities written in your formula, rather than converting a combined egg weight. Whole eggs include the white and yolk already paired in each egg. Extra whites and extra yolks are ingredients listed separately, so they belong in separate fields.
Calculator fieldWhat to enter
Whole eggsThe number of whole eggs in the recipe.
Extra egg whitesWhites listed separately from whole eggs.
Extra egg yolksYolks listed separately from whole eggs.
Enter zero for a field your recipe does not use. Do not add the yolk from each whole egg to the extra-yolk field. Keeping that split lets the calculation show liquid or powder, water for powder, and oil only where it is needed.

secciones.h2: Three eggs, two whites and one extra yolk
secciones.texto:
Use the three entries exactly as the formula states. Here, the 3 whole eggs account for both parts of those eggs. The separate yolk appears only once, as its own ingredient. The calculator adds the amounts below and shows the oil apart from the aquafaba.
Recipe entryLiquid aquafabaPowderWaterOil
3 whole eggs135g9g135 ml0g
2 extra whites60g4g60 ml0g
1 extra yolk15g1g15 ml10g

A 30g powder pouch covers the 14g result. Make up that 14g with 210 ml of water before you add it to the recipe.

secciones.h2: Each part of the egg goes in its own way
secciones.texto:
Whole eggs change the water balance, because aquafaba contains more water than a whole egg. When you replace whole eggs, start by reducing the recipe's other liquids by 5 to 10%. For 200 ml of milk, begin with 180 to 190 ml. Do not apply that reduction when you are replacing only extra whites.

Make powder up with its stated water first. That water stays as given, even when the recipe also needs a whole-egg adjustment. Whip the portion standing in for whites on its own when the method calls for whipped whites. Keep the 10g oil used for an extra yolk out of any foam, then add it where the yolk's richness belongs.

secciones.h2: Choose the pouch that covers your recipe
secciones.texto:
Let the calculator's powder result set the minimum powder pouch. A 30g pouch replaces 15 egg whites, a 200g pouch replaces 100, and a 3kg pouch replaces 1,500. For the worked conversion, 14g fits in the 30g pouch.

For liquid batches, 1L replaces 33 egg whites, 10L bag-in-box replaces 330, and 1T IBC replaces 33,000. If you make up a full powder pouch, 200g takes 3L of water and makes 3.2kg, while 3kg takes 45L and makes 48kg. Make only the aquafaba your batch needs.

faq.question: How do I enter whole eggs and extra whites when I convert a recipe?
faq.answer: Enter whole eggs in the whole-egg field and whites listed separately in the extra-white field. A whole egg already includes its own white and yolk.

faq.question: Do I count the yolk inside each whole egg again?
faq.answer: No. A whole-egg entry already includes its yolk and white. Use the extra-yolk field only for yolks listed separately in the recipe.

faq.question: How much aquafaba do I need for 3 whole eggs, 2 whites and 1 yolk?
faq.answer: Use 210g of liquid aquafaba plus 10g of oil. For powder, use 14g made up with 210 ml of water, plus 10g of oil.

faq.question: How do I replace an extra yolk when I need richness?
faq.answer: Use 15g of liquid aquafaba with 10g of oil for each extra yolk. The powder option is 1g of powder made up with 15 ml of water, plus 10g of oil.

faq.question: Should I reduce milk or other liquids when I replace eggs?
faq.answer: Reduce other liquids by 5 to 10% when you replace whole eggs. If you are replacing only extra whites, leave the recipe's other liquids as they are.

faq.question: Can I add the powder straight into my mix?
faq.answer: No. Make up the powder with water before adding it to the recipe. For one egg white, 2g of powder made up with 30 ml of water makes 32g of aquafaba.

faq.question: Which pouch do I use when my calculator result is 14g of powder?
faq.answer: Use a 30g powder pouch. It covers 14g and replaces up to 15 egg whites when made up with water.

end.cierre: Enter the three egg counts from your next formula, then choose liquid or powder. If you use powder, make it up with the calculated water before mixing. Keep any oil for separate yolks out of the whipped portion, then select the pouch that covers the amount you need.

intro.title: Aquafaba powder dacquoise for almond bases
intro.description: Make almond dacquoise bases from aquafaba powder with batch quantities, reconstitution, frame baking guidance, and pouch choices for your pastry schedule.
intro.h1: Aquafaba powder dacquoise for almond bases
intro.texto:
When your pastry section bakes almond dacquoise bases twice a week, you may not want to open a 1L carton for each frame. One dacquoise batch takes 250g of aquafaba: make up 16g of powder with 240 ml of water, then weigh 250g. That gives you the batch amount without adding powder dry to the mix.

Make the aquafaba up with water first, chill it to 4 to 6 °C, then whip it for a recipe built on whipped egg whites. Fold the whipped aquafaba in, then bake the base in a frame or ring. The working recipe uses sugar, icing sugar, ground almonds, baking powder and cornflour. It contains almonds, so handle the finished recipe to suit your own allergen process. Use the same weighed setup whether you bake a single frame or repeat the base across service.

secciones.h2: How much powder does one dacquoise batch take?
secciones.texto:
Work from the made-up aquafaba weight, not from dry powder. The almond dacquoise formula uses 250g of aquafaba, which is about the equivalent of eight egg whites. Mix 16g of powder with 240 ml of water to make 256g, then weigh 250g into the batch.

The same base also takes 90g of sugar, 250g of icing sugar, 250g of ground almonds, 5g of baking powder and 75g of cornflour. A quantity calculator helps when the number of frames changes, but the individual batch target remains 250g. Almonds are part of the recipe, so record that allergen in your production process.

secciones.h2: How do you make it up for a nut meringue?
secciones.texto:
Powder needs water before it goes near the nut meringue. For this batch, add 16g of powder to 240 ml of water, then take 250g of the made-up aquafaba for the formula. Do not add the powder dry.

Chill the made-up aquafaba to 4 to 6 °C before whipping. Dacquoise is built on a whipped egg-white method, so whip the aquafaba and fold it in. Keep the sugar, ground almonds, icing sugar, baking powder and cornflour as the recipe specifies. That keeps made-up aquafaba as the measured ingredient in the batch.

secciones.h2: What changes when you bake several frames?
secciones.texto:
When several frames are on the bake list, the formula for each base stays the same. Make up the powder with water for the batches you have planned, then weigh 250g of aquafaba into every mix. Do not add dry powder to a larger nut meringue mixture.

Each batch uses 90g of sugar, 250g of icing sugar, 250g of ground almonds, 5g of baking powder and 75g of cornflour. Bake each base in a frame or ring at 200 °C for 10 minutes. Ground almonds remain an allergen in every frame, regardless of whether the aquafaba began as powder.

secciones.h2: Which pouch fits how often you make it?
secciones.texto:
Choose a pouch from the number of batches you expect to make, rather than the size of one mix. A 30g pouch covers one dacquoise batch and leaves 14g. A 200g pouch covers 12 batches.

For regular larger-volume production, a 3kg pouch makes 48kg of aquafaba when made up with 45L of water. The 30g, 200g and 3kg pouches replace 15, 100 and 1,500 egg whites respectively. After opening, keep powder dry and closed until the best-before date printed on the pouch. Match the remaining powder to your next planned bake.

faq.question: How much aquafaba powder do I need for one almond dacquoise batch?
faq.answer: Make up 16g of aquafaba powder with 240 ml of water, then weigh 250g for the batch. The made-up quantity is 256g, and 250g is about the equivalent of eight egg whites.

faq.question: Can I add aquafaba powder straight into my dacquoise mix?
faq.answer: No. Make the powder up with water first, then use the weighed aquafaba in the recipe. Powder is never added dry.

faq.question: Should I chill the made-up aquafaba before I whip it?
faq.answer: Yes. Chill the aquafaba to 4 to 6 °C before whipping it. Dacquoise uses a whipped egg-white method, so whip the aquafaba and fold it in.

faq.question: How do I scale the mix when I bake several dacquoise frames?
faq.answer: Keep the same batch formula for each frame and weigh 250g of made-up aquafaba into every mix. Bake each base in a frame or ring at 200 °C for 10 minutes.

faq.question: Which aquafaba powder pouch should I use if I make dacquoise regularly?
faq.answer: A 30g pouch covers one batch, while a 200g pouch covers 12 batches. A 3kg pouch suits larger regular production and makes 48kg of aquafaba with 45L of water.

end.cierre: Set the number of frames on your bake list, calculate the aquafaba weight, and make up only that amount with water. Then weigh 250g into each dacquoise batch, keep any opened pouch dry and closed, and choose the pouch size that matches how often you bake.

intro.title: Aquafaba powder marshmallows for pastry chefs
intro.description: Make aquafaba powder marshmallows with clear batch quantities, reconstitution timing, multi-frame planning, and pouch choices for confectionery work each day.
intro.h1: Aquafaba powder for marshmallows
intro.texto: With the syrup climbing toward 121 °C, one marshmallow batch needs 100g of aquafaba ready to whip. Make up 7g of powder with 105 ml of water, then weigh 100g for the batch. Set out that made-up aquafaba before the syrup reaches temperature. Keep the powder and water beside the scale before you start the syrup, and make up only the aquafaba the batch needs. That measured preparation keeps the quantity clear whether you are setting one frame or planning several, so pouch choice follows your planned batch count on the bench. Our coconut recipe combines whipped aquafaba with cooked syrup and a carrageenan gel, has 35g of toasted coconut in the mix, pours syrup at 95 °C, holds the gel at 80 °C, and sets the mixture in a frame, with coconut listed as a nut in the recipe.

secciones.h2: How much powder does one marshmallow batch take?
secciones.texto:
Start from the finished aquafaba weight, not the dry powder weight. Our marshmallow recipe uses 100g of aquafaba in each batch. Make up 7g of powder with 105 ml of water to produce 112g, then weigh 100g into the mixture.

That 100g is just over three egg whites' worth. Keep the powder measurement and the made-up aquafaba measurement separate on your production sheet. The powder is the starting ingredient, while the made-up aquafaba is the quantity that goes into the marshmallow formula. Measure the syrup, gel and other ingredients against the recipe you are making.

secciones.h2: When do you make up the powder in the method?
secciones.texto:
Make up the powder with water before the syrup reaches its cooking temperature. In the coconut marshmallow recipe, the syrup cooks to 121 °C and is poured at 95 °C, so the aquafaba should already be measured and ready to whip while the pan is on the heat.

Add the powder to water first. Never put it dry into the mixing bowl. Make up the amount required for the batch, then use the weighed aquafaba in the method. The coconut recipe also includes a carrageenan gel held at 80 °C.

secciones.h2: How do you plan several frames?
secciones.texto:
Start the frame plan with 100g of aquafaba for every batch you intend to set. Then choose the pouch from the number of batches in the run. A 30g pouch covers four marshmallow batches, while a 200g pouch covers 28 batches.

Keep the batch count beside the number of frames so the aquafaba is measured before production starts. The coconut version has 35g of toasted coconut in the mix and is set in a frame. Coconut is listed as a nut in that recipe, so retain that ingredient note with the batch record. Each batch begins with the same 100g aquafaba requirement.

secciones.h2: Which pouch suits a confectionery bench?
secciones.texto:
Choose the pouch from the number of marshmallow batches you have planned. A 30g pouch covers four batches, which suits a shorter run. A 200g pouch covers 28 batches. When you make up a full 200g pouch, it takes 3L of water and makes 3.2kg of aquafaba.

A full 3kg pouch takes 45L of water and makes 48kg of aquafaba, so choose it when your planned production matches that make-up volume. Unopened powder keeps for at least 12 months at room temperature. Once opened, keep the pouch dry and closed until its best-before date.

faq.question: How much aquafaba powder do I need for one marshmallow batch?
faq.answer: You need 7g of powder made up with 105 ml of water. This produces 112g of aquafaba, from which you weigh 100g for the marshmallow batch.

faq.question: Should I add aquafaba powder dry to my marshmallow mix?
faq.answer: No. Make up the powder with water first, then use the made-up aquafaba in the recipe. Powder is never added dry to the mixing bowl.

faq.question: When should I make up the aquafaba before cooking the syrup?
faq.answer: Make it up with water first and have it ready to whip before the syrup reaches 121 °C. In the coconut recipe, the syrup is poured at 95 °C.

intro.title: How much aquafaba per month for pastry?
intro.description: Plan a month of egg-free pastry using batch inputs for meringues, mousse, macarons and pavlova, with storage checks and pack coverage for your menu plan.
intro.h1: How much aquafaba per month for pastry?
intro.texto: For 2 meringue batches and 3 chocolate mousse batches each week, plan 660g per week, about 2.6kg across four weeks. That production pattern replaces 88 egg whites. When you are laying out the month’s bake list, this is the number to check before you open a carton. Enter each weekly batch of meringue, chocolate mousse, macarons, and pavlova, then set the number of weeks you are planning. The planner turns those entries into weekly and monthly aquafaba weight, egg-white equivalents, and pack coverage. It also helps you separate fast-moving production from slower weeks, because opened liquid keeps for 3 to 4 days at 2 to 6 °C. Use it as a pre-batch check, then choose liquid or powder around the production rhythm you already run.

secciones.h2: Enter the batches you make each week
secciones.texto: Start with the batches that appear on your weekly production sheet, not with a pack size. In this planner, one meringue batch uses 150g of aquafaba, one chocolate mousse batch uses 120g, one macaron batch uses 120g, and one pavlova batch uses 150g. Enter the count for each product, including a zero when that item is not scheduled. Then enter the number of weeks in the production month. The planner shows the aquafaba required per week and per month, plus the egg whites replaced at 30g per egg white. That gives you one common measure when the pastry section changes from week to week.

secciones.h2: What does a typical month add up to?
secciones.texto: Monthly planning starts with the weekly total, then applies the weeks you enter. With 2 meringue batches and 3 chocolate mousse batches each week, the planner returns 660g per week. Across four weeks, that is 2.64kg and 88 egg whites replaced. This concrete check is useful when meringue production rises while mousse drops, because you can change only the batch counts and retain the same planning method. A month need not contain the same mix every week. Use the counts on the production plan, rather than assuming that every pastry item calls for the same amount of aquafaba.

secciones.h2: Will an opened carton be used in time?
secciones.texto: Set the opening day beside the work scheduled for the following 3 to 4 days. Opened liquid aquafaba keeps for 3 to 4 days at 2 to 6 °C, so the check is the amount you will use before the next opening day, not the full month total. If the next few days include meringues, mousse, macarons, or pavlova, add those batches together before opening liquid. For a slower week, powder may suit the timing better. Once opened, powder stays usable until the best-before date when the pouch is kept dry and closed. Keep the format decision tied to the schedule, then update it when the bake list changes.

secciones.h2: Which packs cover the month?
secciones.texto: Match the monthly egg-white replacement count to the format you can use on schedule. A 1L Tetrapak replaces 33 egg whites, while a 200g powder pouch replaces 100. For the four-week example, the 200g pouch covers the 88 egg whites in the plan. Larger production can be checked against the 10L bag-in-box, which replaces 330 egg whites, or 3kg of powder, which replaces 1,500. A 30g powder pouch replaces 15 egg whites for a smaller requirement. Choose liquid where the opened-carton window fits the bake list, and use a powder format where the month has slower production days.

faq.question: How do I calculate how much aquafaba I need for a month of pastry?
faq.answer: Enter your weekly batches of meringue, chocolate mousse, macarons, and pavlova, then enter the number of weeks in the month. The planner returns the aquafaba needed per week and per month, along with the egg whites replaced.

faq.question: If I make meringues and mousse each week, how much aquafaba do I need?
faq.answer: For 2 meringue batches and 3 chocolate mousse batches each week, the requirement is 660g per week. Over four weeks, that adds up to 2.64kg and replaces 88 egg whites.

faq.question: Can I use an opened liquid carton for my next pastry production day?
faq.answer: Opened liquid aquafaba keeps for 3 to 4 days at 2 to 6 °C. Check the batches scheduled between the opening day and the next production day before choosing a liquid format.

faq.question: Should I use powder when I have a slower pastry week?
faq.answer: Powder can suit slower weeks when the planned liquid use does not fit the 3 to 4 day opened-carton window. Once opened, keep the pouch dry and closed until its best-before date.

faq.question: Which pack do I use if my month replaces 88 egg whites?
faq.answer: A 200g powder pouch replaces 100 egg whites, so it covers an 88 egg-white monthly requirement. A 1L Tetrapak replaces 33 egg whites and works where its opened use fits the production schedule.

end.cierre: Set the number of weeks, enter the batches on your production plan, and compare the weekly liquid draw with the 3 to 4 day opened-carton window. Then use the pack finder to match the monthly egg-white replacement count to a liquid or powder format before you pre-batch.

intro.title: Aquafaba water content formulation guide
intro.description: Learn how to balance aquafaba water content in an egg replacement formula, adjust other liquids, run a trial batch, and record repeatable production settings.
intro.h1: How do I balance aquafaba water content in a formulation?
intro.texto: Aquafaba carries 90 to 95% water, against about 75% in a whole egg. When you replace whole eggs, start by reducing the recipe's other liquids by 5 to 10%. Your first egg-free sponge or brioche dough can look looser before it reaches the oven. That change often starts at the liquid balance, not at the mixing stage. Use the egg replacement amount as the fixed point, then make a controlled first adjustment to milk, water, or another liquid already in the formula. A whole egg replacement starts at 45g of liquid aquafaba, while an egg white replacement starts at 30g. If you are replacing egg whites only, leave the other liquids unchanged. Powder is made up with water before it enters the mix, so that make-up water stays as specified. The sections below show where to remove water, how to set up the batch, and what to record.

secciones.h2: How much water does aquafaba bring compared with egg?
secciones.texto:
Whole egg replacement changes the water balance because liquid aquafaba contains more water than a whole egg. Use the egg count to set the replacement amount, then adjust the other liquids as the starting move.
Starting point for 4 whole eggs
Original formulaStarting replacement
4 whole eggs180g liquid aquafaba
200 ml milk180 to 190 ml milk
For this worked example, begin the milk adjustment at 180 to 190 ml rather than changing several liquids at once. The whole egg converter helps set the swap. Use whole egg substitutes to check the egg function you are replacing.

secciones.h2: Where do you take the water out of the formula?
secciones.texto:
Take the reduction from a liquid whose decrease you can assess in the first batch. In a milk-based sponge, milk is often the practical starting point. If the formula has more than one liquid, make the initial change in one place rather than spreading small reductions across several ingredients.

Keep the water used to make up powder exactly as given. It belongs to the powder preparation, not to the 5 to 10% reduction. Where you are replacing egg whites rather than whole eggs, leave the formula liquids unchanged. You can compare aquafaba with egg white fairly before deciding which egg function is changing.

Use the recipe converter before you issue the adjusted batch sheet.

secciones.h2: How do you run the first trial batch?
secciones.texto:
Begin with a short product brief: what you make, expected volume, country, and format. Then request the technical sheet and certificate of analysis, and arrange a sample through a qualified enquiry. These documents are sent on request.

Run the first batch in your own formula and on the process that matters for release. For fat-rich batters, mix aquafaba with sugar before it meets fat. If the original method uses whipped egg whites, whip aquafaba and fold it in. The aquafaba baking guide covers these handling points, while aquafaba in food manufacturing puts the trial in a production context.

After you assess the batch against your criteria, move to quote and supply through the distributor for your country. You can test and order for production when the formulation is ready for that step.

secciones.h2: What do you record so the result can be repeated?
secciones.texto:
A repeatable result starts with a batch record that lets you isolate the water change from every other process choice. Record the original formula, the egg replacement amount, the liquid removed, and whether the aquafaba was liquid or powder made up with water.
  • Ingredient order and mixing method
  • Whether sugar met aquafaba before fat
  • Whipping and folding steps, where used
  • Batch observations at the points your specification checks
  • Any formula change made after the first trial
Keep the control formula beside the adjusted version. That gives you a clear basis for the next batch and for the production record.

faq.question: How much liquid should I remove when I replace whole eggs in my formula?
faq.answer: Start by reducing the recipe's other liquids by 5 to 10%. For 200 ml of milk, the starting range is 180 to 190 ml. Keep this as a first trial adjustment, then record what changes in your product.

faq.question: When should I leave the other liquids unchanged?
faq.answer: If you replace egg whites only, leave the other liquids as they are. The water adjustment described here applies when whole eggs are replaced.

faq.question: How do I use aquafaba powder without adding unplanned water?
faq.answer: Make powder up with water before it goes into the formula, never add it dry. Use 2g with 30 ml water per egg white, or 3g with 45 ml water per whole egg. That make-up water stays as specified.

faq.question: Where should I add aquafaba in a fat-rich batter?
faq.answer: Mix aquafaba with sugar before it meets the fat. This order applies to fat-rich batters. If the original formula depends on whipped egg whites, whip aquafaba and fold it in.

faq.question: What do I need to record from my first egg-free batch?
faq.answer: Write down the replacement amount, the liquid you removed, ingredient order, and mixing method. Note whether you used liquid or made-up powder, as well as observations at each point your specification checks. Keep the original and adjusted formulas together.

faq.question: How do I take my aquafaba formulation from trial to production?
faq.answer: Start by sharing what you make, expected volume, country, and format. A qualified enquiry can lead to the technical sheet, certificate of analysis, and a sample for a product trial. After you assess the trial against your criteria, quote and supply proceed through the distributor for your country.

end.cierre: Start with one controlled whole egg replacement and adjust one existing liquid by the stated range. Put the original and adjusted formulas on the same batch sheet. When you are ready to run your product trial, send the product brief with what you make, volume, country, and format.

intro.title: Aquafaba foaming, binding or emulsifying
intro.description: Choose aquafaba's role before scaling a formula: foam, binding or emulsifying. Get workable methods, recipe uses and verified starting ratios for development.
intro.h1: Aquafaba foaming, binding or emulsifying: which job?
intro.texto: At the bench, we start by deciding what the egg does before anything is weighed: whip aquafaba for foam, use it unwhipped for binding, or blend it with oil to emulsify. For a mayonnaise-style emulsion, start with 60g aquafaba to 300g oil. A plated meringue, a rich cake batter and a mayo test can all begin with the same ingredient, but they ask it to do different work. VERY AQUAFABA is filtered, refined and standardized chickpea cooking water made from water and chickpeas. That consistency lets you set the method around the job instead of treating every egg replacement as a whip. Use the egg's function as your brief: air retention, structure in the bake, or a water and oil mix. Then choose when it enters the bowl, how you mix it, and the dose you test.

secciones.h2: Which job does the egg do in your recipe?
secciones.texto:
Read the original formula as a set of egg jobs. An egg white points to aeration. A whole egg usually points to binding in a baked formula. A yolk-led mixture points to an emulsion, with added oil where its richness matters. Start each conversion at the applicable ratio, then test the method in the finished recipe.
JobTypical recipesHow aquafaba goes inDose
FoamMeringue, mousse, cocktailsWhipped30g per egg white
BindingBakingUnwhipped45g per whole egg
EmulsionMayonnaiseBlended with oil15g plus 10g oil per yolk

secciones.h2: How do you use aquafaba when it has to foam?
secciones.texto:
Foam needs air built before the recipe moves on. Chill the aquafaba to 4 to 6 °C before whipping. When a formula is built around whipped egg whites, whip the aquafaba first and fold it into the remaining mix.

For a meringue trial, use 150g aquafaba and 150g sugar. Chill the liquid to 4 °C, whip it for 3 to 5 minutes, then bake at 90 °C for 1.5 to 2 hours. That batch makes about 30 meringues, giving you a defined scale for a first production test.

secciones.h2: How do you use it when it has to bind?
secciones.texto:
Binding is the right route when the egg is there to hold a bake together rather than create a whipped structure. Keep the aquafaba unwhipped. For a formula built around whole eggs, begin at 45g liquid aquafaba per egg and check the batter after the normal mixing sequence.

Fat changes the order of addition. In fat-rich batters, mix the aquafaba with the sugar before it meets the fat. This keeps the conversion aligned with the baking method. Where the original recipe relies on whipped whites, treat that as a foam job instead and whip before folding.

secciones.h2: How do you use it when it has to emulsify?
secciones.texto:
An emulsion calls for aquafaba and oil to be blended together, not whipped as a meringue base. For mayonnaise, use 60g aquafaba with 300g oil, plus 10g mustard, 5g salt and 20g lemon juice. This makes about 500g.

Keep the finished mayonnaise at 4 to 6 °C and use it within 7 days. If the yolk's job in another formula is richness as well as emulsifying, use 15g aquafaba plus 10g oil per yolk as your starting conversion. Keep that test separate from the foam method.

faq.question: How do I know whether to foam, bind, or emulsify with aquafaba?
faq.answer: Start by identifying what the egg contributes to the finished formula. Whipped egg white means a foam method, a whole egg in a bake means binding, and yolk used with oil means an emulsion. Treat each role as a separate conversion.

faq.question: How much aquafaba do I use for egg whites in my meringue?
faq.answer: Start with 30g liquid aquafaba for each egg white. For five egg whites, use 150g aquafaba with 150g sugar. Chill it to 4 °C before whipping.

faq.question: Should I chill aquafaba before I whip it?
faq.answer: Yes, chill aquafaba to 4 to 6 °C before whipping. For the meringue method, chill it to 4 °C and whip for 3 to 5 minutes. This is the foam route, not the method for a bound batter or mayonnaise.

faq.question: How do I use aquafaba in my fat-rich cake batter?
faq.answer: Keep the aquafaba unwhipped when it is replacing the binding role of whole egg. In a fat-rich batter, mix it with the sugar before it meets the fat. Start the whole-egg conversion at 45g aquafaba per egg.

faq.question: How do I make mayonnaise with aquafaba in my development kitchen?
faq.answer: Use 60g aquafaba with 300g oil, 10g mustard, 5g salt and 20g lemon juice. The formula makes about 500g. Keep it at 4 to 6 °C and use it within 7 days.

faq.question: How do I use aquafaba for foam in my cocktail formula?
faq.answer: Measure 20 ml VERY AQUAFABA per drink with a jigger. Dry shake for 10 to 15 seconds without ice, then shake for 10 to 15 seconds with ice. This uses aquafaba as a foam ingredient, not as a binder or emulsion base.

end.cierre: Take one egg-led formula from your current development queue and write the egg's job beside each use. Set the matching starting ratio, then run a foam, binding or emulsion trial with the final process you intend to use before adjusting the rest of the formula.

intro.title: Aquafaba vs Egg White Test Guide
intro.description: Run a fair aquafaba vs egg white test with matched batches, clear pass criteria, controlled handling and practical records for pastry, cocktails and product
intro.h1: How to run an aquafaba vs egg white test fairly
intro.texto: At the pass, the bar station or the development bench, replace one egg white with 30g of aquafaba and change nothing else. That is how you make an aquafaba vs egg white test fair: use one control recipe and decide your pass criteria before you start. Pastry chefs may watch lift and finished texture. Bartenders may follow the head from dry shake through service. Developers may need a record that separates the ingredient from the method. We set the recipe, sugar, equipment, bowl, temperature, timing and operator before the first batch. Then we log foam volume, stability and finished texture against criteria you chose for that product. Use this process for a meringue, a sour or a formulated product, then decide what to test next from the notes.

secciones.h2: What makes the comparison fair?
secciones.texto:
The comparison is fair when the ingredient is the only planned difference. Start from one control formula, whether it is a meringue, a sour or a development prototype. Keep the recipe and every handling condition fixed, then replace each egg white with 30g of aquafaba.

Do not alter sugar to help one batch, change bowls midway or assign different people to each version. Those changes make the notes harder to attribute. Label the samples before you begin and add their preparation order to the trial sheet. A control batch is not a target for aquafaba to copy. It is the reference that lets your own criteria show whether the replacement suits that particular application.

secciones.h2: Which criteria do you set before the test?
secciones.texto:
Set the pass line before you open either ingredient. A pastry test may put volume and finished texture on the sheet. A bar test may focus on the head, handling and how it holds through the serve. A development trial may need process notes another operator can follow.
What stays fixedWhat you measureHow you record it
Recipe, sugar, equipment, bowl, temperature, timing and operatorFoam volume, stability over service and texture of the finished productOne trial sheet, batch labels and notes at the same checkpoints
Keep the wording specific enough that you can mark each batch without changing the criteria afterward. Use pass, review or fail only when those terms match the decision you need to make.

secciones.h2: How do you run the two batches side by side?
secciones.texto:
Prepare both batches from the same formula and keep the bowl and equipment choice fixed between runs. Weigh the aquafaba at 30g for each egg white in the control recipe. Keep one operator, the same timing and the same handling sequence for both versions.

For a cocktail method using aquafaba, measure 20 ml with a jigger, dry shake, then shake with ice. Do not change another ingredient or the mixing method halfway through the comparison. Give each sample a code before you assess it, then record observations in the order set on your sheet. If you repeat the test, repeat both batches under the same criteria rather than retesting only one version.

secciones.h2: How do you read the result?
secciones.texto:
Read the result against the pass criteria you set, not against a general expectation about either ingredient. Put the batch sheets side by side and review volume, stability and finished texture separately. This helps you see where a result met the brief and where it did not.

Keep observations distinct from decisions. “The head held through service” is an observation. “Suitable for this sour specification” is a decision based on the criteria you chose. If a result falls outside those criteria, do not adjust one sample afterward to close the gap. Note the condition you want to change, then run a new matched pair. Your record can then show whether to move forward, revise the method or test a different application.

faq.question: How do I replace one egg white in my test?
faq.answer: Use 30g of aquafaba for one egg white. Keep every other ingredient and handling condition fixed so the replacement is the only planned difference.

faq.question: How do I set pass criteria for a pastry aquafaba test?
faq.answer: Write the criteria before you mix either batch. You may record volume, shape and finished texture, then decide what counts as pass, review or fail for that recipe.

faq.question: How do I test aquafaba in a sour against egg white?
faq.answer: Build matched drinks from the same recipe and keep the handling sequence consistent. For the aquafaba cocktail method, measure 20 ml with a jigger, dry shake, then shake with ice.

faq.question: How do I keep my aquafaba trial consistent across operators?
faq.answer: Have one operator run both batches where possible. If you need another session, keep the recipe, sugar, equipment, bowl, temperature, timing and record sheet unchanged.

faq.question: How do I record foam stability in my comparison?
faq.answer: Choose the checkpoints before the test and use them for both samples. Record what you observe at each checkpoint, then keep that observation separate from your pass or fail decision.

faq.question: How long can I keep opened liquid aquafaba for a second test?
faq.answer: Opened liquid aquafaba keeps for 3 to 4 days at 2 to 6 °C. Record when you opened it so the second trial uses liquid stored within that period.

end.cierre: Write the control recipe and your pass criteria on one sheet, then schedule the two batches under the same conditions. Start with the application that matters most in your service or development work. Once you have recorded the result, choose one next test rather than changing several variables at once.

intro.title: Aquafaba vs egg white sour bar test
intro.description: Run an aquafaba vs egg white sour test with the same recipe, shake and glass. Compare foam, taste and service method before you update your sour menu.
intro.h1: How do I test aquafaba vs egg white in a sour?
intro.texto: At the menu meeting, make the same sour twice: one with egg white and one with 20 ml of VERY AQUAFABA. Use the same recipe, jigger, shake and glass, then judge both drinks side by side before you change a sour on the menu. This is a bar test, not a guess from the pack. Keep the spirit, citrus and syrup identical, and give each drink the same dry shake and shake with ice. Look at the head as it lands, return to it after a few minutes on the bar, and taste each sour. Then ask the bartender making it what felt clear or awkward at the station. We use 20 ml per drink, measured with a jigger. For a pisco sour trial of 40 drinks, that means 1,600 ml of pisco, 800 ml of lime juice and 800 ml of aquafaba.

secciones.h2: How do you set up the test?
secciones.texto: Choose one sour that already has a settled spec at your bar. Make two versions in the same service window: your current egg white build, then the aquafaba build. Keep the spirit, citrus, syrup and glass unchanged, so you are testing the foamer rather than a new drink. Measure the aquafaba with the same jigger you use for the rest of the build. Dry shake each drink for 10 to 15 seconds without ice, then shake for 10 to 15 seconds with ice. Start with a whiskey sour or pisco sour you know, and compare aquafaba with egg white fairly by writing the method down before the first pour.

secciones.h2: What do you look at in the glass?
secciones.texto:
Pour both drinks into the same glassware you use for that sour, without changing the rest of the serve. Look at each drink as it lands, then leave both on the bar for a few minutes. Taste them in turn before you discuss a menu change.
What to compareWhat to note
Head after pouringHeight, coverage and bubble appearance
Head a few minutes laterWhat remains in each glass
TasteHow each finished sour tastes side by side
MethodHow the bartender found the sequence at the station
Do not reduce the trial to a photo of the first head. The point is to compare what is in front of you, including the bartender's handling of the method.

secciones.h2: How do you test it during a real service?
secciones.texto: Run the comparison when tickets are coming in, not only during a prep session. Pre-batch the spirit, citrus and syrup if that is how you work, but add the aquafaba at the shake, never to the batch. Keep the trial bottle at 2 to 6 °C, mark the opening date and use opened liquid within 3 to 4 days. Ask each bartender who makes a trial drink to follow the same written sequence. Note where the jigger sits, whether the dry shake is being skipped, and what happens at the pass. Keep cocktail process and checks close to the station, then record whether the method supports the same foam from every bartender during the shift.

secciones.h2: What happens after the test?
secciones.texto: Put the two records beside the existing sour specification after service. If you decide to make another trial, change one thing at a time and repeat the same checks. If you decide the aquafaba method belongs on the menu, write 20 ml into the spec and keep the shaking sequence beside it. Use the trial notes to plan how you would replace egg whites on a cocktail menu, including where the liquid is stored and when it is added. Do not fold it into a citrus batch. A clear station note gives anyone making the sour the same starting method.

faq.question: How much aquafaba should I pour into the sour I am testing?
faq.answer: Use 20 ml of VERY AQUAFABA per drink, measured with a jigger. Hold the rest of the recipe steady so the side-by-side test focuses on the foamer.

faq.question: How should I shake the aquafaba sour in my trial?
faq.answer: Dry shake for 10 to 15 seconds without ice, then shake for 10 to 15 seconds with ice. Use the same sequence for both test drinks.

faq.question: Can I pre-batch the aquafaba with my sour mix?
faq.answer: No. You can pre-batch the spirit, citrus and syrup, but add the aquafaba at the shake. Keep it out of the batch during the trial and in your written method.

faq.question: What should I look for when I compare the two glasses?
faq.answer: Check the head after the pour and again after a few minutes on the bar. Taste both drinks, then record how the bartender found the method at the station.

faq.question: Will I taste chickpea in the sour I test?
faq.answer: There can be a light roasted note in the pack. When it is shaken into a drink, that note disappears, so taste both finished sours side by side.

faq.question: How do I get a sample for the bar trial I am planning?
faq.answer: Send a qualified enquiry with the sour you want to test. We serve every country through distributors, reply within two working days, and send a sample in reply to a qualified enquiry.

end.cierre: Choose one sour and schedule a side-by-side pour before the next menu decision. Write the recipe, glass, shake sequence and observations on one sheet. If you need liquid for a qualified bar trial, send an enquiry with the sour you plan to test.

intro.title: Aquafaba bakery trial for cakes, sponges and meringues

intro.h1: How do I run an aquafaba bakery trial?
intro.texto: Start with the recipe you sell most, replace each egg at 45g per whole egg or 30g per white, and bake it beside your current version. For the morning sponge that has to look the same on Monday and Friday, this keeps the comparison close to the product your line already knows. Use the same handling and oven program. Keep formula changes limited to the egg replacement and, where needed, the water adjustment. An aquafaba bakery trial works when you set the question before mixing: are you checking volume, crumb, slice, shell, or a combination? Cakes, whipped sponges and meringues use aquafaba differently, so give each product its own test plan. secciones.h2: Which recipe do you test first?
secciones.texto: Start with the recipe you sell most. A whole-egg cake, a sponge built on whipped whites and a meringue each need a different handling check, so keep the first trial to one egg role. When whole eggs are replaced, aquafaba brings more water into the formula. Start by reducing the other liquids by 5 to 10%, then assess the baked result against your own criteria. If you use aquafaba powder, make it up before mixing. It goes into the bowl as liquid, never dry.

intro.title: Aquafaba mayonnaise production trial guide

intro.h1: How to test aquafaba mayonnaise for production
intro.texto:
With your current mayonnaise on the bench, start aquafaba mayonnaise production with 60g of aquafaba to 300g of oil, a 5 to 1 ratio. Keep the oil and acid identical to your current sauce so the comparison stays focused on the emulsion. Add 10g of mustard, 5g of salt and 20g of lemon juice for a reference batch of about 500g.

Run this as a controlled kitchen trial, not a recipe swap made halfway through service. Record how the emulsion comes together, what it looks like after chilling and how it behaves in the finished sauce. Then repeat the same formula before moving to a larger pre-batch. The aquafaba removes egg from this part of the formula, but you still need to check every other ingredient in the sauce.

secciones.h2: How do you set up the first emulsion trial?
secciones.texto:
Use the same mixer and vessel you use for your current sauce. Add the aquafaba, mustard, salt and lemon juice, then introduce the oil gradually while you mix. Keep the oil, acid and process consistent with your existing mayonnaise so you are testing the egg-free emulsion rather than several recipe changes at once.

Record the trial while you make it. Those notes give you a useful reference when you repeat the formula or review a larger batch.

Chill the finished sauce, then assess it against the way you plan to use it. Check whether it holds together, how it sits on a spoon or in a squeeze bottle, and whether any oil becomes visible. Taste it beside your current sauce, using the same oil and acid in both samples.

Keep the trial mayonnaise at 4 to 6 °C and use it within 7 days. Aquafaba removes egg from the formula, but that does not describe the whole sauce. Check mustard, oil, acid and every other ingredient before making a vegan or allergen statement. Chickpea and other legume allergies can still exist.

Once the reference batch holds across repeated trials, use the 500g formula as your control point. Keep the 60g aquafaba to 300g oil ratio, then scale the other ingredients in the same proportion. Change one part of the process at a time, rather than changing the recipe and the equipment in the same run.

Make a pre-batch using the same mixer, ingredient sequence, oil and acid. Record what changes when you work at your intended volume, including how the sauce behaves after chilling. Keep each batch at 4 to 6 °C and use it within 7 days while you assess the process.

secciones.h2: Which documents can you ask for?

When a purchasing file or quality review is open, you can ask for a technical data sheet and a certificate of analysis. They are separate records with different jobs. The technical sheet is the product-level document. The COA is the batch-level document.

Before you decide whether to take a sample into development, the technical sheet gives you the product description to review. It covers product identity and ingredients, product characteristics, average nutritional values, allergen information, microbiological criteria, storage conditions, shelf life and product codes.

This is the document for assessing the recurring specification, not a record of a single production batch. It gives purchasing, quality and development a common reference for their review. Use it alongside your own acceptance criteria, then retain it with the records used for product approval. The document is sent on request with a qualified enquiry, and no parameter values are reproduced here.

secciones.h2: What does a certificate of analysis tell you?

Match the COA to the batch identification on delivery records before you complete your incoming-goods process. This keeps a batch-specific check separate from the technical sheet that describes the product more broadly. The certificate does not replace the technical sheet, and the technical sheet does not identify checks on a particular production batch. Do not use quoted values from another batch as evidence for the one you receive.

We set that rule around the station, not around who happens to be on it. Write the measure, the shake order and the batch boundary where each bar can check them before service and at handover. Pre-batch the spirit, citrus and syrup when it suits service, then add aquafaba only at the shake. intro.title: Egg-free cocktails for restaurant groups
intro.description: Plan egg-free cocktails across every bar with a shared spec, bartender training, stock rules and ordering steps built for multi-site restaurant groups.
intro.h1: How to introduce egg-free cocktails across a restaurant group
intro.texto: During service, one bar is still cracking eggs while another is already calling for a sour specification. Switch the sours that already use egg white, using 20 ml of VERY AQUAFABA per drink and one written method for every site. Start with the serves your bartenders already know, then make the change repeatable rather than asking each venue to interpret it. A group rollout needs a short drink list, a measured pour, a shake sequence and a local stock plan. We keep the foamer out of the pre-batch and add it at the shake. That lets each bar follow the same core routine while planning its own volume from its own sales. VERY AQUAFABA contains no egg, dairy, gluten or soy. Chickpea is not among the 14 allergens covered by EU mandatory allergen labelling, although chickpea and other legume allergies can still exist. Check every other ingredient before making an allergen statement about a finished drink.

secciones.h2: Which drinks do you switch first?
secciones.texto: Start with named sours that already call for egg white, not every foamed serve on day one. Your menu review can identify the drinks where a like-for-like station change makes sense. Our recipes use 20 ml of VERY AQUAFABA in Pisco Sour, Amaretto Sour, Whiskey Sour, Gin Fizz, White Lady, La Rosée and The Sunset. Keep the first group small enough that each site can test the written routine during normal service. Record the drink name, the existing build and the glass your bar already serves its sours in. Do not add a new garnish or presentation rule unless it belongs in the menu specification.

secciones.h2: How do you write the specification every site follows?
secciones.texto: The specification should fit on a station card. For each sour, write the drink name, ingredients, pour measures, aquafaba measure, shake order, glass and any existing garnish. State that the spirit, citrus and syrup are pre-batched, while aquafaba is added at the shake. Specify 20 ml measured with a jigger for every drink. This keeps the foamer separate from the batch and gives a site manager clear checks at handover. Use the same wording and order at every venue, then retain a local recipe only where its menu build differs. Version the card so an old printout is not treated as current.

secciones.h2: How do you train the bartenders on the method?
secciones.texto: Train from the card at the station, using one full drink from the menu. Measure 20 ml with a jigger, dry shake without ice for 10 to 15 seconds, then shake with ice for 10 to 15 seconds. Have each bartender repeat the same sequence with the relevant sour. The check is observable: the measured pour goes in at the shake, not in the pre-batch, and both shake stages happen in order. Keep the card beside the tools while the method is new. Managers can review the drink during a normal shift and correct the step, rather than asking for a different technique by site.

secciones.h2: How do you order for the group?
secciones.texto: Order by the sales pattern at each site. A 1L Tetrapak makes 50 drinks at 20 ml per drink, so use each venue's own sour sales to set its order. Do not roll one outlet's volume across the group. Once opened, liquid keeps for 3 to 4 days at 2 to 6 °C, and the opening date needs marking. Unopened liquid and powder keep at least 12 months at room temperature. We serve every country through distributors. If the group buys across borders, put the countries, formats and delivery contacts in one enquiry. Recurring orders can then follow the pattern each site establishes.

faq.question: How do I choose the first egg-free cocktails for my restaurant group?
faq.answer: Start with sours that already use egg white and already have a clear recipe at every site. Pisco Sour, Amaretto Sour, Whiskey Sour, Gin Fizz and White Lady are suitable starting points in our cocktail recipes. Keep the first rollout focused on drinks that your bartenders already make.

faq.question: What should I put in one specification for every site?
faq.answer: Include every measured ingredient, the 20 ml aquafaba pour, the pre-batch instruction and the two shake stages. State that aquafaba is added at the shake, rather than put into the spirit, citrus and syrup batch. Add the existing glass and garnish only where they are part of that drink's current build.

faq.question: How do I teach bartenders the same shake method?
faq.answer: Demonstrate the routine with a jigger and one menu sour. Dry shake without ice for 10 to 15 seconds, then shake with ice for 10 to 15 seconds. Keep the written card at the station so bartenders can follow the same order during service.

faq.question: How much VERY AQUAFABA should I order for each site?
faq.answer: Use that site's own sour sales, not a group-wide average. A 1L Tetrapak makes 50 drinks when each drink uses 20 ml. Consider the number of sites, each menu's sour mix and the storage routine at each bar.

faq.question: How do I store opened liquid at each bar?
faq.answer: Store opened liquid at 2 to 6 °C and mark the opening date. It keeps for 3 to 4 days after opening. Unopened liquid and powder keep at least 12 months at room temperature.

faq.question: Can I describe every egg-free cocktail as vegan or allergen-free?
faq.answer: The foam, yes: VERY AQUAFABA is plant-based and egg-free. The pisco, the lime and the syrup carry their own labels. VERY AQUAFABA contains no egg, dairy, gluten or soy, but chickpea and other legume allergies can still exist. Check every ingredient before making a vegan or allergen statement about the finished drink.

intro.title: Aquafaba for busy bar service

intro.h1: How to use aquafaba during a busy cocktail service
intro.texto: At 11 pm on Saturday, when a queue of sour tickets lands at the well, keep the base pre-batched and add aquafaba only at the shake. Measure 20 ml per drink with a jigger, then dry shake before shaking with ice. That split keeps the bottle work simple when orders stack up. Your spirit, citrus and syrup can be ready in the batch, while the foamer stays under your control on every ticket. Set the carton where you can reach it without crowding the tins, then return it to the fridge between rounds. The workflow suits Pisco Sours, Whiskey Sours, Amaretto Sours, Gin Fizzes and other drinks that need the same measured foamer step. Keep the jigger in one fixed place, so the last step of every sour stays repeatable at service pace.

secciones.h2: How do you set up the well before the rush?

Before doors, give aquafaba one fixed position beside the shaker tins and the jigger. Keep chilled liquid ready for the service you expect, rather than leaving every carton at the well. Dry shake for 10 to 15 seconds without ice, then shake for 10 to 15 seconds with ice. Keep that order the same for every ticket, whether you are making a White Lady, Gin Fizz or Whiskey Sour. Batch the spirit, citrus and syrup only. Aquafaba goes into the shaker at the point of service, never into the batch. This keeps the batch bottle focused on the base while you control the foamer drink by drink.

When a ticket prints, pour the batch, measure the aquafaba with the jigger, then follow the dry shake and ice shake sequence. Once opened, keep liquid aquafaba at 2 to 6 °C and use it within 3 to 4 days. Mark the opening date on the carton. Close it and put it back in the fridge between rounds, rather than leaving it on the well through the whole shift.

The liquid formats include the 1L Tetrapak and 10L bag-in-box. An unopened liquid carton keeps for at least 12 months at room temperature, so you can keep unopened stock away from the active station. During service, only the carton you are using needs to come out for the measured pour.

faq.question: How much aquafaba should I pour for each sour when I am slammed?

faq.question: Can I use this for a vegan sour on my cocktail list?

Set the guest count, then separate the base from the foamer, so the shake station has one measured pour for every order. We cover the quantities for 100, 200 and 300 welcome sours, the two-part shake, and the way to handle liquid left in opened cartons.

Set your count around one welcome sour per guest, then reserve 20 ml of aquafaba for each drink. A 1L Tetrapak makes 50 drinks, which gives you a direct check before the banquet begins. This count assumes each guest receives one welcome sour.

Build the sour base from the spirit, citrus and syrup before the banquet. Keep aquafaba out of that batch. It belongs in the shaker as a separate measured 20 ml pour.

Mark each opened carton with the opening date and hold it at 2 to 6 °C. Opened liquid keeps for 3 to 4 days. Keep unopened liquid at room temperature until you need it, it keeps at least 12 months.

If a banquet leaves liquid that you will not use within that window, freeze aquafaba at −18 °C or lower in 30g or 50g portions. Thaw portions overnight in a refrigerator at 2 to 6 °C. Do not refreeze thawed aquafaba.

faq.question: How long can I keep opened aquafaba cartons after my banquet?

intro.title: Replace Egg White on Your Cocktail Menu

intro.h1: How do you replace egg white on a cocktail menu?
intro.texto: At the first busy service after a menu change, replace every sour that uses egg white with 20 ml of VERY AQUAFABA. That rule covers the egg-white builds already on your list, from a house sour to a Pisco Sour, and gives you the same jigger measure for each specification. Start by mapping every egg-white drink, then rewrite the line item rather than redesigning the drink. You can retain the spirit, citrus and sweetener build you already serve, while documenting the foamer and shake sequence beside it. For a seasonal bar, the same menu decision also changes what you hold during quieter weeks. We set out the audit, specification edit, menu language and stock choices so you can make the change one drink at a time.

secciones.h2: Which drinks on your menu use egg white?

Pull the current spec book or POS build and mark each drink where egg white appears. Look beyond drinks called a sour: a Whiskey Sour, Amaretto Sour, Gin Fizz and White Lady are familiar places to check, alongside house signatures and short seasonal serves. Do not add a foamer to drinks that never called for egg white. The aim is to replace the ingredient where the existing build needs it.

Create one audit line for every affected drink: drink name, current spirit, acid, sweetener, egg white, glass and method. This shows what stays fixed when you remove egg white. The whiskey sour and amaretto sour give two useful specifications to review before editing your own list.

secciones.h2: How do you rewrite each specification?

Change the foamer line in each affected specification to 20 ml of VERY AQUAFABA, measured with a jigger. Leave the rest of that drink’s stated build in place unless you are making a separate recipe decision. A Pisco Sour provides a clear template: 40 ml pisco, 20 ml lime juice, 20 ml cane syrup and 20 ml VERY AQUAFABA.

Write the method under the ingredients: dry shake for 10 to 15 seconds without ice, then shake for 10 to 15 seconds with ice. Run the sour test in your bar on every revised drink before it returns to the list. This lets you compare the written build with the served drink instead of relying on a memory of the old specification.

secciones.h2: What do you tell guests on the menu?

Your menu can name aquafaba plainly and describe the drink’s actual ingredients. For example: “Pisco Sour, pisco, lime, cane syrup and aquafaba.” That tells a guest what is in the glass without turning an ingredient note into a broad claim about the full drink.

VERY AQUAFABA contains no egg, dairy, gluten or soy. Chickpea is not among the 14 allergens covered by EU mandatory allergen labelling, but chickpea and other legume allergies can still exist. intro.title: Aquafaba foam cocktail service: a bar guide

intro.h1: How do I maintain aquafaba foam throughout cocktail service?

At the first run of sour tickets, the head comes from 20 ml measured every time and a dry shake before the ice. Keep that measure in each tin, then shake without ice for 10 to 15 seconds before shaking with ice for 10 to 15 seconds.

That routine gives you a checkable process when the first Pisco Sour and the last Whiskey Sour are far apart. We add aquafaba at the shake, not to the pre-batch. Keep the carton at 2 to 6 °C between rounds, and mark the date when you open it. When a head looks weak, return to those steps before changing the pour. secciones.h2: What builds the foam in the shaker?

Foam is made in the shaker at the point you build the drink. Measure 20 ml with a jigger for every serve. Dry shake without ice for 10 to 15 seconds, then shake with ice for 10 to 15 seconds.

The same measure is used in a Pisco Sour, Amaretto Sour, Whiskey Sour, Gin Fizz, White Lady, La Rosée, and The Sunset when you use VERY AQUAFABA. Pre-batch the spirit, citrus, and syrup for service. Add the aquafaba only when that drink reaches the shaker, so the measured pour and shake sequence stay with the individual order.

secciones.h2: What weakens it during a long service?

Long service makes the routine easier to lose track of as tins, tickets, and open cartons move through the station. Keep the aquafaba pour at 20 ml rather than altering it from drink to drink. Put the carton back in the fridge between rounds and keep it at 2 to 6 °C.

An opened carton keeps for 3 to 4 days at that temperature, so the opening date belongs on the carton. If the head changes, return to the measured pour, the dry shake, and the marked storage window first. Those are the preparation checks to make before you change the dose.

Use the same check order every time a sour looks different from the previous one. Look at preparation first, not a larger pour. This keeps the next action tied to something you can see or read on the carton.

secciones.texto:
Open a new carton when the current one is outside its 3 to 4 day opened window at 2 to 6 °C. Read the date on the carton before the first round, and mark each newly opened carton. That date gives you a clear point to check during a busy shift.

faq.answer: Pre-batch the spirit, citrus, and syrup. Add the aquafaba when you shake each individual drink.

faq.question: How long can I use an opened aquafaba carton?
faq.answer: Opened liquid keeps for 3 to 4 days at 2 to 6 °C. Mark the opening date and return the carton to the fridge between rounds.

faq.question: What should I check if I see a weak head?
faq.answer: Check that you dry shook before adding ice, measured 20 ml with a jigger, and kept the carton within its 3 to 4 day opened window at 2 to 6 °C. Check those steps before changing the dose.

faq.question: Will I taste chickpeas in my sour?
faq.answer: There is a light roasted note in the pack. When it is shaken into a drink, that note disappears.

end.cierre: Before the next busy round, set a jigger beside the tins, write the opening date on the carton, and return it to the fridge between shakes. Run the same dry shake and ice shake sequence for each sour. If you are planning regular service with VERY AQUAFABA, send an enquiry with the drinks you make.
