intro.title: Consistent cocktail foam for every bartender
intro.description: Train every bartender on one consistent cocktail foam method: the jigger measure, shake order, station checks and carton rules that keep service aligned.
intro.h1: How to get consistent cocktail foam across your bar
intro.texto: At the pass, two Pisco Sours can leave with different heads when the build shifts between bartenders. We use one rule for consistent cocktail foam: the same jigger, 20 ml per drink, the same dry shake and the same timings. You can put that rule on every station instead of relying on a verbal handover. Foam changes when a pour is free-handed, the aquafaba is added to a pre-batch, or the ice stage is skipped. Write the build in one order, then check a new bartender against that card before service. Use one sour as the training drink, such as a Pisco Sour or Whiskey Sour, so each check covers the same ingredients and shake sequence. Your aim is not to judge a drink by guesswork. It is to make the measured steps visible, repeatable and easy to correct.

secciones.h2: Why does the head change from one bartender to another?
secciones.texto:
Variation starts before the tins meet the ice. One bartender can use the jigger while another free-pours, and the liquid amount is no longer the same. The build also changes when aquafaba is mixed into a pre-batch instead of added at the shake.

Keep the spirit, citrus and syrup together in the pre-batch. Add the aquafaba during the shake, then follow the dry-shake and ice-shake order every time. A Pisco Sour and a Whiskey Sour can share the same control points, even when their base spirits differ. The goal is one visible method, rather than a bartender's personal sequence.

secciones.h2: How do you write the method down?
secciones.texto:
The card should show the actions in the order you expect to see them. Keep it beside the tins and use the drink name at the top, so a bartender does not borrow a step from another sour. We use this four-part card for each listed foam drink:
  • 1. Pre-batch the spirit, citrus and syrup.
  • 2. Measure 20 ml of aquafaba with the jigger and add it at the shake.
  • 3. Dry shake without ice for 10 to 15 seconds.
  • 4. Add ice and shake for 10 to 15 seconds.
Do not add unmeasured alternatives to the card. If a step changes, update the same card used in training and at the station.

secciones.h2: How do you check a new bartender's drink?
secciones.texto:
Watch a full build, not only the finished glass. Ask the bartender to follow the card without prompts, then compare the measure, when aquafaba enters and both shake stages with the written sequence.

Use one drink for the check, so you are looking at the same method each time. If a step differs, point to that step and have the bartender repeat the build. This keeps the conversation on a visible action, such as the jigger or dry shake, rather than a personal preference. Record the method change on the card before it becomes a different habit.

secciones.h2: How do you keep the same jigger and carton rules?
secciones.texto:
The jigger and carton rule need to be as clear as the shake rule. Use the same jigger for the 20 ml measure and keep it where the foam drinks are built. A 1L Tetrapak makes 50 drinks at that measure, which lets you match stock handling to the card.

Once opened, keep the liquid at 2 to 6 °C for 3 to 4 days and mark the opening date. Check that mark before the shift begins. If the carton moves between stations, move the label with it. The carton and the jigger are part of the method, not separate back-bar decisions.

faq.question: How do I stop free-pouring aquafaba?
faq.answer: Put the jigger on the written card and make it the only measure used for aquafaba. Each listed foam cocktail uses 20 ml, so a free pour sits outside the method.

faq.question: What do I put on my cocktail foam method card?
faq.answer: Write the drink name, the pre-batch ingredients, the 20 ml aquafaba measure and both shake stages. The card should also state that aquafaba is added at the shake, not into the pre-batch.

faq.question: Can I pre-batch aquafaba for my sour?
faq.answer: Pre-batch the spirit, citrus and syrup. Add the aquafaba when the drink is shaken, so that step remains part of every bartender's build.

faq.question: How do I check a new bartender's drink?
faq.answer: Watch the full build against the method card. Check the jigger measure, the point when aquafaba is added, the dry shake and the shake with ice before discussing the finished drink.

faq.question: Which shake timings do I use for my foam drinks?
faq.answer: Dry shake without ice for 10 to 15 seconds. Then add ice and shake for another 10 to 15 seconds.

faq.question: How do I manage an opened 1L Tetrapak?
faq.answer: Mark the opening date and keep the liquid at 2 to 6 °C for 3 to 4 days. At a 20 ml measure, one 1L Tetrapak makes 50 drinks.

end.cierre: Choose one sour from your current menu and put the four-step card at each station. Watch one full build per bartender against the card, then correct the measure, shake order or carton handling before the next service. Once the card is settled, use the same format for the rest of your foam drinks.

intro.title: Aquafaba powder cocktails: service prep
intro.description: Learn how to make up aquafaba powder for cocktail service, measure 20 ml per drink, plan service volume, chill it, and choose when powder suits your bar.
intro.h1: How to prepare aquafaba powder for cocktails
intro.texto: At the sour station before service, make up 2g of powder with 30 ml of water for 32g of aquafaba. Chill it, then measure 20 ml per drink, just as you would with the liquid format. Powder goes into water first, never into the shaker dry. For 40 pisco sours, that is 1,600 ml of pisco, 800 ml of fresh lime juice and 800 ml of aquafaba. Make up only what the service needs, then use the same jiggered pour and shake routine your bar already knows. That keeps prep linked to covers, the sour list and the pace of that shift. Make a second small batch when service calls for it, rather than working from a weekly batch. Dry shake each drink first, then shake it with ice. This guide covers the ratio, the service quantity and when powder fits the way your bar works.

secciones.h2: How do you make up powder for a service?
secciones.texto:
Measure the water and powder separately, then make them up before you build any cocktails. The working ratio is 2g of powder with 30 ml of water, giving you 32g of made-up aquafaba. Once it is chilled, treat it as the aquafaba pour for your service.

Use 20 ml in each drink and measure it with a jigger. Do not add dry powder to the shaker or straight into a pre-batch. Dry shake the cocktail first, then shake it with ice. Keep the instructions to make up the powder beside your prep sheet so the ratio stays clear at the station.

secciones.h2: How much do you make up?
secciones.texto:
Start with the number of sours you expect to serve and allow 20 ml of made-up aquafaba for each drink. For a run of 40 pisco sours, prepare 800 ml of aquafaba. Make that amount for the service, not for the week.

The powder calculator helps you turn a drink count into the amount of powder and water to set aside. Choose a 30g pouch or a 200g pouch around the quantity your bar expects to make up, without treating either format as a drinks-per-pouch target. If orders change during service, make another small batch rather than preparing a large one in advance.

secciones.h2: How do you keep the made-up aquafaba during service?
secciones.texto:
Keep the made-up aquafaba chilled during service and pour each cocktail measure with a jigger. Prepare it for the shift in front of you, rather than holding a made-up batch for the week. This keeps the station focused on the quantity you are actually using.

Store unopened powder at room temperature. Once opened, keep the pouch dry and closed until its best-before date. The guide on how to store aquafaba behind the bar can help you set the unopened pouch and the made-up batch in the right parts of your station. Keep dry powder separate from the water until you are ready to make it up.

secciones.h2: When does powder suit your bar?
secciones.texto:
Powder suits a bar where sour orders change from one service to the next and you want to make up the working quantity before doors open. It also fits a station that needs a dry pouch stored until the next planned service. The made-up aquafaba is then poured at the same 20 ml measure used for liquid aquafaba.

Choose the format around your service pattern, your expected sour count and how often you need to make a fresh batch. Read aquafaba powder in cocktails for the wider cocktail method, including the dry shake followed by the shake with ice. Use powder when the make-up routine fits how your bar prepares its sours.

faq.question: How do I make up aquafaba powder before I open the bar?
faq.answer: Make up 2g of powder with 30 ml of water to produce 32g of aquafaba. Chill it before service and use it as your measured cocktail pour.

faq.question: How much made-up aquafaba do I pour into each cocktail?
faq.answer: Pour 20 ml of made-up aquafaba per drink. Measure it with a jigger, then dry shake the cocktail before shaking it with ice.

faq.question: Can I put the powder straight into my shaker?
faq.answer: No. Make up the powder with water first, then use the made-up aquafaba in the cocktail. Dry powder is not added directly to the shaker.

faq.question: How do I hold made-up aquafaba during my service?
faq.answer: Keep the made-up aquafaba chilled during service. Make only the amount you expect to use for that service, rather than preparing a weekly batch.

faq.question: How do I choose a powder pouch for my bar?
faq.answer: Choose between a 30g pouch and a 200g pouch based on the quantity you expect to make up for service. Both use the same make-up ratio and the same 20 ml cocktail measure.

faq.question: Is the foam plant-based and egg-free when I use the powder?
faq.answer: The foam, yes: VERY AQUAFABA is plant-based and egg-free. The pisco, the lime and the syrup carry their own labels.

end.cierre: Write down the number of sours you expect for your next service. Set aside 20 ml of made-up aquafaba for each one, prepare that amount before doors open and chill it. Run it through your usual dry shake and ice shake. If you need help choosing a pouch or preparing for more than one bar, send an enquiry.

intro.title: How to store aquafaba behind the bar
intro.description: Store liquid and powdered aquafaba in a compact back bar. Learn fridge, freezer, opening checks, and weekend stock planning for busy sour service in small bars.
intro.h1: How to store aquafaba behind the bar
intro.texto: At the start of a packed sour service, space behind the bar disappears fast. Opened liquid aquafaba keeps for 3 to 4 days at 2 to 6 °C. Unopened liquid aquafaba and powder keep for at least 12 months at room temperature. Once opened, powder keeps until its best-before date when the pouch stays dry and closed. That gives you a clear split for a tight back bar. Keep sealed formats at room temperature, chill only the liquid carton in use, and keep opened powder in dry storage. Measure 20 ml of VERY AQUAFABA with a jigger for each drink. A 1L Tetrapak makes 50 drinks, so you can match the carton you open to the service you expect. Check the open carton each shift, return it to the fridge after pouring, and freeze unused liquid in portions when needed.

secciones.h2: Where should you keep each format?
secciones.texto:
Give the fridge space to liquid aquafaba only after opening. Sealed liquid cartons and sealed powder pouches can stay at room temperature, which leaves chilled storage for fresh juice, syrups, and the carton currently on the station.
FormatUnopened storageAfter opening
Liquid aquafabaRoom temperature for at least 12 monthsClose after use and keep at 2 to 6 °C for 3 to 4 days
PowderRoom temperature for at least 12 monthsKeep the pouch dry and closed until its best-before date
Use a 1L Tetrapak when you expect regular sour orders. Keep powder as dry reserve stock, then follow the steps to prepare powder for cocktails when you need it.

secciones.h2: How do you check opened packs before service?
secciones.texto:
Run this check before the first sour leaves the bar, then repeat it whenever you pick up the carton during service. It takes a moment and tells you whether the open liquid is still suitable to pour.
  1. Look at the liquid and the carton before measuring.
  2. Smell the aquafaba before adding it to a drink.
  3. Throw it away if it has a sour smell, bubbles in the pack, or a separated look.
  4. Close the carton after every use and put it straight back in the fridge.
Mark the opening date on the carton as soon as you break the seal. That label lets you check the 3 to 4 day chilled window without trying to remember which shift opened it.

secciones.h2: What can you do when an opened carton will not be finished?
secciones.texto: If an opened carton is unlikely to be finished during its chilled window, freeze the remaining liquid in 30g or 50g portions. Keep those portions at −18 °C or lower for up to 3 months. Small portions let you thaw the amount you expect to use rather than opening another carton. Thaw a portion overnight in the fridge at 2 to 6 °C. Never refreeze thawed aquafaba. Use the guidance to store and freeze aquafaba for the full routine, or check whether you can freeze aquafaba for a specific storage question. For the opened-carton window, see how long aquafaba keeps after opening.

secciones.h2: How should you organize stock for a busy weekend?
secciones.texto:
Start with the number of sour drinks you expect to serve, then calculate liquid at 20 ml per drink. Keep unopened cartons at room temperature and open only the amount that fits your likely service. Powder can stay dry and closed as reserve stock when fridge space is already spoken for.
Expected drinksLiquid aquafaba needed
10 drinks200 ml
25 drinks500 ml
50 drinks1L
100 drinks2L
Use the bar reorder planner before ordering. Keep the opening date visible on every active carton, especially when service runs across several days.

faq.question: How long can I keep an opened liquid carton at my bar?
faq.answer: Keep opened liquid aquafaba for 3 to 4 days at 2 to 6 °C. Mark the opening date, close the carton after each use, and return it straight to the fridge.

faq.question: Can I keep unopened aquafaba outside my bar fridge?
faq.answer: Yes. Unopened liquid aquafaba and unopened powder keep for at least 12 months at room temperature. This lets you reserve fridge space for the liquid carton currently in use.

faq.question: How do I store an opened powder pouch behind my bar?
faq.answer: Keep the opened powder pouch dry and closed. It keeps until the best-before date printed on the pouch.

faq.question: What should I do if I notice bubbles or a sour smell in my carton?
faq.answer: Throw the liquid away if it has a sour smell, bubbles in the pack, or a separated look. Check the carton before service and before you measure it into a drink.

faq.question: Can I freeze liquid aquafaba if I will not finish the carton?
faq.answer: Yes. Freeze opened liquid aquafaba in 30g or 50g portions at −18 °C or lower for up to 3 months. Thaw it overnight in the fridge at 2 to 6 °C, and never refreeze it.

faq.question: How much liquid aquafaba should I plan for my sour menu?
faq.answer: Measure 20 ml of VERY AQUAFABA per drink with a jigger. A 1L Tetrapak makes 50 drinks, so 100 drinks need 2L.

end.cierre: For your next order, count the sours you expect to serve, set aside only the liquid carton you expect to finish within its chilled window, and label it when opened. Keep powder dry as reserve stock. If you are planning for more than one bar or need format details, send an enquiry with your expected drink volume.

intro.title: Cocktail station prep for aquafaba sours
intro.description: Set up a cocktail station for aquafaba sours with measured pours, pre-batched bases, cold storage and end-of-night checks for a consistent service routine.
intro.h1: How to prepare a cocktail station for aquafaba sours
intro.texto: Before the first tickets land, set a dedicated sour lane with your aquafaba, jigger, tins, ice access and labeled bases. Keep the aquafaba out of every batch and measure 20 ml per drink at the shake, so each sour follows the same station routine. A packed rail exposes small gaps fast. A carton left at the wrong temperature, a jigger parked across the well or a base bottle without a clear place interrupts the build. Set the station so the sequence stays visible: pick up the base, measure the aquafaba, dry shake, add ice, then shake again. This setup works across Pisco Sours, Whiskey Sours, White Ladies and the other sours you already pour. We make ready-made chickpea aquafaba for this part of service, but the station discipline matters as much as the carton.

secciones.h2: What goes on the station before service?
secciones.texto:
Build the lane before the first call, not while a sour ticket is waiting. Put clean shaker tins, a Hawthorne strainer, a jigger and a clear route to ice in the order you use them. Keep the carton in its cold holding spot, then bring it to hand only for the pour.
ItemWhereCheck
CartonFridgeOpening date marked, held at 2 to 6 °C
JiggerNext to shaker tinsClean and ready for 20 ml
Pre-batched baseReachable station positionSpirit, citrus and syrup only
Shaker tinsStart of the sour laneClean and ready to dry shake
Use one station pattern for every sour on your list. That gives you a visible check before the shaker leaves the rail, rather than asking yourself where an ingredient or tool went mid-round.

secciones.h2: How do you place the aquafaba and the jigger?
secciones.texto:
Keep the opened carton in the fridge at 2 to 6 °C. Set the jigger beside the shaker tins, on the hand you use to build the drink. That layout lets you measure the aquafaba just before the dry shake, rather than pouring by eye.

Date the carton when you open it. Return it to the fridge between rounds, even when the rail is busy. Measure 20 ml into the tin, dry shake for 10 to 15 seconds without ice, then shake for 10 to 15 seconds with ice. Keep the jigger clear of syrup residue so its measure stays readable.

secciones.h2: How do you set the pre-batched bases?
secciones.texto:
Set pre-batched bases where you can reach them without crossing the sour lane. Build each base with the spirit, citrus and syrup. Leave aquafaba out of the bottle, because it goes into the shaker at the time of the shake.

For 40 Pisco Sours, that's 1,600 ml of pisco, 800 ml of fresh lime juice and 800 ml of aquafaba. Keep the aquafaba portion separate from the batch and measure it as each order is made. Label the base with the drink name, then position the carton and jigger beside it. The same rule applies whether you are preparing a Whiskey Sour, Amaretto Sour, Gin Fizz or White Lady.

secciones.h2: What do you check at the end of the night?
secciones.texto:
Close the station with the carton first. Check that its opening date is visible and that it has gone back into the fridge. Opened liquid keeps for 3 to 4 days at 2 to 6 °C, so the date is part of the close-down check, not an afterthought.

Rinse and put away the jigger, shaker tins and strainer. Remove empty base bottles and leave the next service with a clear place for each sour tool. Unopened liquid and powder keep for at least 12 months at room temperature. If you change a build or station order, write the new steps into your process sheet before the next service.

faq.question: How much aquafaba should I measure for each sour?
faq.answer: Measure 20 ml of VERY AQUAFABA for each drink with a jigger. A 1L Tetrapak makes 50 drinks at that measure.

faq.question: Can I put aquafaba in my sour pre-batch?
faq.answer: No. Pre-batch the spirit, citrus and syrup, then add aquafaba in the shaker for each order.

faq.question: Where should I keep an opened carton during service?
faq.answer: Keep an opened carton in the fridge at 2 to 6 °C. Bring it out to measure, then put it back in the fridge between rounds.

faq.question: How long can I keep my opened aquafaba?
faq.answer: Opened liquid keeps for 3 to 4 days when held at 2 to 6 °C. Mark the opening date on the carton so you can check it at close.

faq.question: How should I shake an aquafaba sour on a busy rail?
faq.answer: Dry shake for 10 to 15 seconds without ice after adding the aquafaba. Then add ice and shake for another 10 to 15 seconds.

faq.question: Can I use aquafaba if I need an egg-free foam?
faq.answer: The foam, yes: VERY AQUAFABA is plant-based and egg-free. The pisco, the lime and the syrup carry their own labels.

end.cierre: Before your next service, stand at the rail and run one sour from the labeled base to the fridge return. Move any tool that makes you cross the lane, date the carton when it opens, and keep the 20 ml jigger measure in its fixed place. If you need ready-made aquafaba for your bar, send an enquiry.

intro.title: Aquafaba bottled cocktail guide
intro.description: Learn how to bottle a sour base for later service, add aquafaba at the shake, and set clear storage, label, and station rules for consistent pours at service.
intro.h1: How do I use aquafaba with a bottled cocktail base?
intro.texto: Bottle the spirit, citrus and syrup, then add 20 ml of VERY AQUAFABA at the shake. Keep aquafaba out of the bottled sour base, because it is added only when you finish each drink. At the prep bench, you can bottle a base for later service while keeping one measured foamer step at the station. For 40 pisco sours, that is 1,600 ml of pisco, 800 ml of fresh lime juice and 800 ml of aquafaba. Bottle the pisco, lime and syrup under your own process, then portion the aquafaba for service. This keeps the bottle focused on the sour base and gives the bartender a clear final step. Use the same split when you write the bottle label, service spec and storage instructions.

secciones.h2: What goes in the bottle, and what stays out?
secciones.texto:
Your bottled sour base contains the spirit, citrus and syrup chosen for that drink. VERY AQUAFABA stays separate until service. It is not part of a shelf-stable drink, and it should not go into the bottle when you make the batch.

Give the base bottle the drink name and keep the foamer instruction beside it. The person bottling the base can follow the production spec, while the bartender measures aquafaba into the shaker for every serve. The pack has a light roasted note, but that note disappears once it is shaken into a drink. If you are building repeatable prep, use the same separation when you pre-batch your sours.

secciones.h2: How do you finish the drink at service?
secciones.texto: Pour the portion of bottled sour base set by your own drink spec into a shaker. Measure 20 ml of VERY AQUAFABA with a jigger, then dry shake for 10 to 15 seconds without ice. Add ice and shake again for 10 to 15 seconds. The aquafaba belongs in the shaker before the dry shake, not in the prepared bottle. Keep that instruction visible where the drink is finished, especially when the base moves from a prep area to a service station. A clear mixing order for foamed drinks gives the person making the serve the same sequence every time. A 1L Tetrapak provides 50 measured cocktail serves at 20 ml each.

secciones.h2: How do you label and store the base?
secciones.texto:
Write the base name, its ingredients, its preparation date and your handling instructions on the bottle. Make it clear that the bottle holds the spirit, citrus and syrup base, while aquafaba is added at the shake. Follow your own food-safety rules for the bottled base and its service window.

Keep a separate opened-date mark on the aquafaba used at the station. Opened liquid keeps for 3 to 4 days at 2 to 6 °C. Unopened liquid and powder keep for at least 12 months at room temperature. If you need production documentation for your process, the technical sheet and certificate of analysis are available on request.

secciones.h2: When is a bottled base worth it?
secciones.texto:
A bottled base can suit you when the same sour is prepared repeatedly and you want the batching work completed before service. It separates the bottle preparation from the final shake, without putting aquafaba into the packaged base. The method also gives drinks producers a clear distinction between the bottle formula and the finished-drink procedure.

Start with one sour that you already make often. Record the base formula, the bottle label and the station instruction to add 20 ml of aquafaba. If the format is moving into larger production, build a co-packer brief around that split. You can also review aquafaba for drinks producers before deciding how the foamer step fits your bottling process.

faq.question: Can I put aquafaba in my bottled sour base?
faq.answer: No. Bottle the spirit, citrus and syrup, then add VERY AQUAFABA when you shake each drink. Aquafaba is never presented as part of a shelf-stable drink.

faq.question: How much aquafaba should I add to each bottled cocktail serve?
faq.answer: Measure 20 ml of VERY AQUAFABA per drink with a jigger. A 1L Tetrapak makes 50 drinks at that measured serve.

faq.question: How should I shake a bottled sour base with aquafaba?
faq.answer: Pour your specified base portion into the shaker and add 20 ml of aquafaba. Dry shake for 10 to 15 seconds without ice, then shake for 10 to 15 seconds with ice.

faq.question: How long can I keep opened aquafaba at my service station?
faq.answer: Opened liquid keeps for 3 to 4 days at 2 to 6 °C. Mark the opened date on the service container and keep the bottled sour base under your own handling procedure.

faq.question: What should I put on my bottled sour base label?
faq.answer: Identify the drink, the ingredients in the bottled base, the preparation date and your handling instructions. State separately in the service spec that aquafaba is measured into the shaker, not included in the base bottle.

faq.question: Can I keep my bottled cocktail foam plant-based?
faq.answer: The foam, yes: VERY AQUAFABA is plant-based and egg-free. The pisco, the lime and the syrup carry their own labels.

end.cierre: Take one current sour and write its base formula, bottle label and station instructions on one sheet. Keep the aquafaba step separate, with 20 ml and the two shakes stated plainly. If you want to check that workflow against your own format, request a drinks trial or send an enquiry.

intro.title: Mixing Order for a Foamed Cocktail
intro.description: Learn the mixing order for a foamed cocktail: what enters the tin, when to add aquafaba, why dry shaking matters, and when to top with carbonation last.
intro.h1: What is the mixing order for a foamed cocktail?
intro.texto: Build a foamed cocktail in this order: noncarbonated ingredients, aquafaba, a dry shake, ice, a second shake, then the carbonated top in the glass. At a packed station, keeping that order stops you from reaching for tonic or ice before the foam has had its first shake. Put spirit, citrus, syrup, and other still ingredients in the tin. Measure 20 ml of VERY AQUAFABA with a jigger, then dry shake for 10 to 15 seconds. Add ice and shake again for 10 to 15 seconds. Strain before you top a Gin Fizz with tonic water or The Sunset with ginger beer. The order is simple enough for a station card and keeps the work in the tin separate from the final build in the glass.

secciones.h2: What goes into the tin first?
secciones.texto:
When the ticket lands, begin with every ingredient that is meant to be shaken and has no carbonation. Measure the spirit, citrus, syrup, and any still modifier into the tin. This is also the point to use a pre-batched spirit, citrus, and syrup base if that is how you build sours.

A Gin Fizz gives you a clear station check: 40 ml gin, 20 ml lemon juice, and 20 ml cane syrup go in before the foamer. Keep tonic water away from the tin. Ice waits until after the dry shake, so the first shake works only the liquid ingredients and aquafaba.

secciones.h2: When does the aquafaba go in?
secciones.texto:
Add aquafaba once the base is measured and immediately before the dry shake. Measure 20 ml with a jigger for each drink. This puts the foamer into the shaker at the point where it is ready to be worked with the rest of the liquid.

Pre-batch the spirit, citrus, and syrup, not the aquafaba. Add it during each build instead. Whether you are working from a bottled sour base or measuring each ingredient to order, the aquafaba belongs at the shake. Keep that step visible on the station so it does not get added after ice.

secciones.h2: Why does the dry shake come before the ice?
secciones.texto:
The dry shake comes first because ice does not interrupt the first agitation of aquafaba with the other ingredients. It gives you a defined stage for combining the foamer with the sour base before chilling and dilution begin.

Dry shake without ice for 10 to 15 seconds. Then add ice and shake for another 10 to 15 seconds. Treat these as two separate checks in the build. If ice enters the tin first, you have skipped the dry stage rather than changing its order.

secciones.h2: Where do the carbonated tops go?
secciones.texto:
Carbonated tops belong in the glass after the shaken drink has been strained. Carbonated ingredients are never shaken. For a Gin Fizz, strain into a highball and top with tonic water. For The Sunset, strain into a highball and top with ginger beer.

Keep the top separate from the shaker sequence. It is the final build step, not another ingredient for the tin. That distinction makes the move from shaking to serving clear when you are switching between sours and long drinks during service.

faq.question: What do I put in the shaker first for a foamed cocktail?
faq.answer: Put the spirit, citrus, syrup, and any other still ingredients in the shaker first. Add aquafaba next, before the dry shake. Ice and carbonated ingredients stay out of the tin at this stage.

faq.question: When do I add aquafaba if I pre-batch sours?
faq.answer: Add aquafaba at the shake, after you pour the pre-batched spirit, citrus, and syrup into the tin. Measure 20 ml per drink with a jigger. Do not include aquafaba in the pre-batch.

faq.question: How long should I dry shake my cocktail?
faq.answer: Dry shake for 10 to 15 seconds without ice. Then add ice and shake for another 10 to 15 seconds. Keep both stages in the build order.

faq.question: Can I shake tonic water or ginger beer with aquafaba?
faq.answer: No. Carbonated ingredients are never shaken. Strain the shaken drink first, then add tonic water to a Gin Fizz or ginger beer to The Sunset in the glass.

faq.question: Do I add ice before or after the dry shake?
faq.answer: Add ice after the dry shake. Start with the still ingredients and aquafaba, dry shake, then add ice for the second shake. This keeps the two shake stages distinct.

faq.question: How much VERY AQUAFABA do I use in one drink?
faq.answer: Use 20 ml of VERY AQUAFABA per drink and measure it with a jigger. A 1L Tetrapak makes 50 drinks. Add it after the other still ingredients and before the dry shake.

end.cierre: Write the sequence on your shaker station: still ingredients, 20 ml aquafaba, dry shake, ice shake, strain, then top. Run it through the next Gin Fizz or Sunset build and check that the carbonated ingredient never reaches the tin. If you need ready-made aquafaba for that workflow, send an enquiry.

intro.title: Alcohol-free sour aquafaba menu for bar managers
intro.description: Build an alcohol-free sour menu with aquafaba: choose foamed drinks, test your base, write clear listings, and plan bar stock with practical daily checks.
intro.h1: How do I build an alcohol-free cocktail menu with aquafaba?
intro.texto: With the ticket printer running, an alcohol-free sour takes the same 20 ml of VERY AQUAFABA and the same dry shake as any sour. We keep that station rule checkable: measure it with a jigger before you shake. Build the menu around bases that stay balanced once shaken, then test the exact base you plan to pour. You are not copying a fixed alcohol-free recipe here, because each base needs its own trial. Keep the method consistent, give each drink a clear name, and record the service details beside it. That lets guests choose an alcohol-free sour from the list without creating a separate workflow at the station.

secciones.h2: Which alcohol-free drinks take a foam?
secciones.texto:
Start with drinks you intend to serve in a sour-style format. An alcohol-free sour is the clearest place to use foam because it follows the same aquafaba method as a regular sour: measure, dry shake, then shake with ice. Test the specific base on your list rather than deciding by its name alone.

Use foam when it supports the drink you have tasted and approved at service. VERY AQUAFABA has a light roasted note in the pack, but that note disappears once it is shaken into a drink. Keep an alcohol-free foamer trial focused on the base, the shake and the finished serve.

secciones.h2: How do you build the base?
secciones.texto:
Build each trial from the alcohol-free base you intend to serve, then test it with 20 ml of VERY AQUAFABA measured in a jigger. Dry shake for 10 to 15 seconds without ice, then shake for 10 to 15 seconds with ice. This is the same sequence used for an alcohol-free sour.

Record the base, the menu name and the finished result while you test. If a drink needs a different balance, revise the base and test again rather than changing the foamer measure. Keep the written cocktail process and checks at the station so the drink can be made the same way each time.

secciones.h2: How do you write the menu?
secciones.texto:
Write the drink as an alcohol-free sour when that is the serve you have tested. Keep the wording clear about what the guest is ordering, and do not imply that the whole drink is vegan or allergen-free because it includes aquafaba.

VERY AQUAFABA contains no egg, dairy, gluten or soy. Chickpea is not one of the 14 allergens covered by EU mandatory allergen labelling, but chickpea and other legume allergies can still exist. Check every other ingredient before making any menu statement, and keep the allergen question separate from the foam description. If other people make the drinks, give them the same approved wording.

secciones.h2: How do you plan stock for the alcohol-free list?
secciones.texto:
Count planned alcohol-free sour serves by drink, then map that count to your foamer format. A 1L Tetrapak makes 50 drinks when each one uses 20 ml. Use the bar reorder planner alongside your menu trials so the list and the stock decision stay connected.

Opened liquid keeps for 3 to 4 days at 2 to 6 °C. Unopened liquid and powder keep for at least 12 months at room temperature. Opened powder, kept dry and closed, keeps until its best-before date. Review how often each listed drink is ordered before deciding which format suits your bar.

faq.question: How much aquafaba should I pour when I make an alcohol-free sour?
faq.answer: Use 20 ml of VERY AQUAFABA per drink. Measure it with a jigger so each alcohol-free sour follows the same station rule.

faq.question: How do I shake an alcohol-free sour with aquafaba during service?
faq.answer: Dry shake for 10 to 15 seconds without ice. Then add ice and shake for 10 to 15 seconds. This is the same method used for a sour with aquafaba.

faq.question: Can I foam any alcohol-free drink on my bar menu?
faq.answer: Not automatically. Test the specific base you intend to serve, because an alcohol-free sour has no published fixed recipe on this site. Keep the 20 ml foamer measure and the shake method consistent while you assess the base.

faq.question: How should I describe an alcohol-free sour on the menu?
faq.answer: Use a clear name such as alcohol-free sour when that is the drink you have tested. Do not describe the full drink as allergen-free. Check the base, syrups and every other ingredient before making any dietary statement.

faq.question: Can I call an aquafaba foam vegan or allergen-free?
faq.answer: The foam, yes: VERY AQUAFABA is plant-based and egg-free. The pisco, the lime and the syrup carry their own labels. Do not call the finished drink allergen-free, because other ingredients and individual legume allergies still need consideration.

faq.question: How long can I keep VERY AQUAFABA after opening?
faq.answer: Opened liquid keeps for 3 to 4 days at 2 to 6 °C. Unopened liquid and powder keep for at least 12 months at room temperature. Opened powder, kept dry and closed, keeps until the best-before date.

Put the stated per-drink amount and shake instruction in the service specification, not in the batch formula. This gives the co-packer a clear boundary between what is manufactured and what is added at service. Do not ask the brief to make a claim about finished-drink stability. faq.question: Can I ask my co-packer to add aquafaba to my bottled sour base?
faq.answer: No. Prepare the bottled base without aquafaba, then add it at the shake when serving. Keep the service dose and shake action in instructions outside the manufactured base.

faq.question: How much VERY AQUAFABA should I specify for each drink I serve?
faq.answer: Specify 20 ml of VERY AQUAFABA per drink. It goes in during the shake, never in the batch.

faq.question: How do I get the TDS and COA for my brief?

faq.answer: Start with exploration and specification. A sample in reply to a qualified enquiry comes before a product trial against your criteria, then quote and supply after validation through the distributor for your country.

intro.title: Scale a cocktail recipe to a pilot batch
intro.description: Learn how to scale a cocktail recipe into a pilot batch, set your aquafaba volume, record each shake, and decide the next production step with a pilot sheet.
intro.h1: How do I scale a cocktail recipe to a pilot batch?
intro.texto: Multiply 20 ml of aquafaba by the drinks in your pilot. For 500 drinks, you need 10L, which is one 10L bag-in-box. That gives you a fixed starting point before the first scaled shake. At the bench, a recipe that works for one serve has to become a process someone else can repeat. Scale every ingredient from the same base, keep the aquafaba dose measured with a jigger, and test the drink through the service conditions you expect. This guide shows what to prepare, what to capture during the pilot, and how to move from a working batch to a production discussion. We make ready-made aquafaba for professionals, so the focus stays on your drink, your method, and the decisions the trial needs to support.

secciones.h2: How do you scale the recipe?
secciones.texto:
Start with the exact serve that passed your bench trial. Multiply each component by the planned number of serves, then keep the same sequence at the shake. For 40 pisco sours, that's 1,600 ml of pisco, 800 ml of fresh lime juice and 800 ml of aquafaba. The aquafaba goes in at the shake and is measured with a jigger.

Do not change the drink while you change the batch size. If the pilot needs a different service method or another recipe adjustment, record it as a separate trial condition. That keeps the original recipe distinct from what you are testing next.

secciones.h2: How much aquafaba does the pilot need?

Choose the volume from the pilot plan, not from the amount you happen to have on the bench. 100 drinks take 2L, 250 drinks take 5L, and 500 drinks take 10L. A 500-drink run uses one 10L bag-in-box. Once opened, liquid keeps 3 to 4 days at 2 to 6 °C, so set the run dates before opening the pack. That timing matters when you need repeat shakes or a second service check.

After the pilot, move forward with the version you can describe clearly. With us, the professional route moves through four steps: exploration, specification, a trial in your product with your criteria, then quote and supply after a validated trial through the distributor for your country.

faq.question: How long can I use liquid aquafaba after I open it?
faq.answer: Opened liquid keeps 3 to 4 days at 2 to 6 °C. Plan your pilot dates and repeat checks within that storage window.

faq.question: What should I write down while I am running a cocktail pilot?
faq.answer: Record the recipe version, volumes, planned drink count, aquafaba dose, pack format, and shake sequence. Add the conditions you used and your observations against the criteria for that trial.

faq.question: What do I do if I want to take my pilot recipe into production?
faq.answer: Start by bringing forward the version of the recipe and process you tested. The next stages are exploration, specification, a trial in your product with your criteria, then quote and supply after a validated trial.

intro.title: Cocktail foamer comparison for drink developers
intro.description: Compare cocktail foamers in a controlled aquafaba test. Set equal conditions, judge foam and flavor, then plan a focused drinks trial with clear criteria.
intro.h1: How do I compare cocktail foamers with aquafaba?
intro.texto: At the test bench, compare cocktail foamers by holding the drink and service method steady, then judge the head and taste against your own brief. For VERY AQUAFABA, start with 20 ml per drink, measured with a jigger, and keep each alternative at the dose its own instructions specify. When you are developing a sour or reviewing an egg-free spec, a side-by-side shake tells you more than a single glass. Build a repeatable pour, record what you see just after service and again at the same set later point, then taste each drink without changing its base. We use this approach because a foamer is part of the full drink, not a result viewed in isolation. The comparison can show which trade-offs fit your format, workflow and target serve.

secciones.h2: What do you compare between foamers?
secciones.texto: A cocktail foamer comparison should reflect the drink you intend to serve, not a generic foam score. Put foam height, surface coverage, bubble pattern, stability at a set time, aroma, flavor and handling on one scorecard. Add any requirement that matters to your format, such as a pre-batch process or a particular glass. Keep the drink base and the glass identical while you test. Give each foamer the dose in its own instructions, then record what changes in the finished serve. If egg white is your control, compare aquafaba with egg white fairly under the same conditions. You are looking for a documented fit with your criteria, not a universal winner.

secciones.h2: How do you set up the test?

Dose each product as its own instructions say. With VERY AQUAFABA, measure 20 ml with a jigger, dry shake for 10 to 15 seconds without ice, then shake for 10 to 15 seconds with ice. Serve each sample in the same glass and record the conditions without adjusting the shake to rescue one result. You can run the sour test in your bar when you want a working protocol for a service-led comparison.

secciones.h2: How do you judge the head and the taste?
secciones.texto: Assess the head as a service outcome, not just as a photograph. Check it directly after pouring, then at the same set time for every glass. Record relative height, coverage, bubble appearance, drainage and any visible breaks. Taste the drink after the visual check, using the same drink build for each sample. VERY AQUAFABA has a light roasted note in the pack. Shaken into a drink, it disappears. Capture that distinction in your notes rather than judging from the pack alone. Our cocktail foamer guidance can help you frame the test around the pour you are developing.

secciones.h2: How do you request a trial sample?

We then move to specification, including the technical sheet and certificate of analysis. A sample follows a qualified enquiry. Next, trial VERY AQUAFABA in your product using your own criteria. Quote and supply come after a validated trial. If your question comes before the trial brief, send an enquiry and state what you need to evaluate.

faq.answer: Keep the drink, glass and shake the same for every sample. Use each foamer at the dose stated in its own instructions, then judge the head after pouring, at a set time, and by taste.

faq.question: How much VERY AQUAFABA should I use in my drink test?
faq.answer: Use 20 ml per drink, measured with a jigger. Hold that dose steady while applying each other foamer's own instructions to its sample.

faq.question: How should I shake VERY AQUAFABA in my sour test?
faq.answer: Dry shake for 10 to 15 seconds without ice. Then shake for 10 to 15 seconds with ice before pouring.

faq.question: What should I write down when I judge a foam head?
faq.answer: Record relative height, coverage, bubble appearance, drainage and visible breaks. Keep one fixed assessment time after pouring so each sample is judged at the same point.

faq.question: Will I taste chickpeas when I test VERY AQUAFABA?
faq.answer: You may notice a light roasted note in the pack. Once it is shaken into a drink, that note disappears.

faq.question: How do I request a VERY AQUAFABA sample for development?
faq.answer: Start with a qualified enquiry that explains your drink, format and test criteria. We then provide the technical information for specification, followed by a sample and trial route where appropriate.

intro.title: Aquafaba meringue production batch trial guide
intro.description: Plan an aquafaba meringue production trial with batch quantities, process checks, recording fields and pack choices for larger pastry production runs now.
intro.h1: How to test aquafaba meringue production at scale?
intro.texto:
You have a larger mixer booked and need an aquafaba meringue production trial that gives you a clear record before a longer run. 150g of aquafaba and 150g of sugar make about 30 meringues, so ten batches take 1.5kg of each for about 300 meringues.

Start with one fixed formula, then increase only the batch count. Keep aquafaba chilled to 4 °C, follow the same whip and bake settings, and write down what happens at each run. That lets you compare a one-batch check with a 5, 10 or 20-batch trial without mixing process changes into the result.

The aim is not to change every variable at once. It is to see whether your planned production conditions hold as the bowl load grows. We set out the quantities, checks, trial record and pack handling you need to plan the run.

secciones.h2: How much aquafaba does a larger batch take?
secciones.texto:
Start with the output you need to inspect, then select a whole number of the site recipe. One batch gives about 30 meringues. Five batches give about 150, ten give about 300, and 20 give about 600. Keep aquafaba and sugar at the same weight for every row.

secciones.h2: What do you check at the new scale?
secciones.texto:
Keep the base method fixed when the bowl load changes. Chill aquafaba to 4 °C, whip for 3 to 5 minutes, and bake at 90 °C for one and a half to two hours. Note the bowl load and oven load, so you can identify which part of the run changed.

Check the foam before it goes into the oven and inspect the baked meringues after cooling. Use the same mixer, whisk, tray setup and baking program where your production plan allows. A meringue process and checks sheet gives each run the same comparison points. If you are preparing to scale pastry batches, decide in advance which observations count as accepted and which call for another trial.

secciones.h2: How do you record the trial?
secciones.texto:
Give every run a batch reference and use a fresh line for every batch. A record that combines several runs can hide a change in handling, equipment load or bake conditions. Keep the same sheet for liquid aquafaba and powder, but record them as separate trials.

  • Batch count, aquafaba format, and weighed aquafaba and sugar
  • Powder and water amounts when using powder
  • Chilled aquafaba temperature, whip time, oven temperature and bake time
  • Mixer, whisk, bowl load, tray setup and oven load
  • Notes on the foam before baking and the meringues after cooling

Write the checks during the run rather than rebuilding the record afterwards. This gives you a traceable basis for the next batch count.

secciones.h2: Which pack feeds the run?
secciones.texto:
Choose the format around your trial schedule and what remains after the run. A 1L Tetrapak replaces 33 egg whites, while a 10L bag-in-box replaces 330 egg whites. A 200g pouch of powder replaces 100 egg whites, and powder can be made up batch by batch with water.

Unopened liquid and powder keep for at least 12 months at room temperature. Once opened, liquid keeps for 3 to 4 days at 2 to 6 °C. Opened powder keeps until its best-before date when it stays dry and closed. These handling points can help you decide whether to stage a liquid run or hold powder for further trials.

faq.question: How much aquafaba do I need for 10 meringue batches?
faq.answer: For 10 batches, use 1.5kg of aquafaba and 1.5kg of sugar. This produces about 300 meringues using the site recipe.

faq.question: Should I test liquid and powder in the same production trial?
faq.answer: You can test both formats, but record them as separate runs. For each batch using powder, make up 10g of powder with 150 ml of water before using it in the meringue formula.

faq.question: What do I keep the same when I scale my mixer load?
faq.answer: Keep the formula, chilled aquafaba temperature, whip time, tray setup and baking settings consistent. The site method chills aquafaba to 4 °C, whips for 3 to 5 minutes, and bakes at 90 °C for one and a half to two hours.

faq.question: How do I record an aquafaba meringue trial?
faq.answer: Record each batch separately, including the format, weighed ingredients, bowl load, whip time and oven load. Add notes on the foam before baking and on the meringues after cooling.

faq.question: Which pack should I use for repeated meringue runs?
faq.answer: A 1L Tetrapak replaces 33 egg whites and a 10L bag-in-box replaces 330 egg whites. A 200g powder pouch replaces 100 egg whites and can be made up in the batch amount you need.

faq.question: How do I store aquafaba after I open it for a trial?
faq.answer: Opened liquid keeps for 3 to 4 days at 2 to 6 °C. Opened powder keeps until the best-before date when it is kept dry and closed.

end.cierre: Choose the 1, 5, 10 or 20-batch count that matches the mixer time you can reserve. Write the check sheet before you weigh the first ingredient, then run one format through your normal meringue process. If you need a technical sheet, certificate of analysis or a sample for a qualified enquiry, send an enquiry to begin the specification step.

intro.title: Aquafaba macarons production for pastry chefs
intro.description: Plan aquafaba macarons production for orders with batch quantities, tray checks, pack choices, and a practical validation run for pastry chefs at volume.
intro.h1: How do you scale aquafaba macarons for professional production?
intro.texto:
At the bench, when an order turns one bowl into a production run, aquafaba macarons production starts with a fixed unit: 120g of liquid aquafaba makes about 40 filled macarons. Ten batches take 1.2kg and make about 400 filled macarons, so scale by repeated batches rather than changing the formula.

That choice keeps your mise en place clear across whipping, macaronage, piping, resting and oven loading. For each 120g liquid batch, use 150g sugar, 150g almond flour and 150g icing sugar. If you work with powder, make up 8g with 120 ml water for the same batch. This guide maps quantities for larger orders, the points to log on each tray, and the pack format that matches the way you schedule production. It also gives you a controlled larger run to review before you put a new volume on the order board.

secciones.h2: How much aquafaba do you need for your macaron production?
secciones.texto:
Begin with the number of filled macarons on the order, then plan in complete batches. This stops a large bowl from becoming a new method to judge during production. The quantities below keep the same formula at each step. If you use liquid, measure the listed aquafaba weight. If you use powder, make it up with the paired water amount before whipping. Use the macaron quantity calculator to set the order quantity, then put the batch count beside every tray plan.

secciones.h2: What do you check when you increase a batch?
secciones.texto:
An increase in volume should leave the checkpoints familiar. Log each check against your approved small-batch method, rather than relying on a single look at the shells at the end of production. Keep the same order of work from whipping through maturation. If any point needs attention, isolate that batch and record where the sequence changed before setting the next run. This gives you a process record for the next order.

secciones.h2: How do you organize several trays without changing the method?
secciones.texto:
Keep the formula in batch units, then organize movement around each tray rather than building a larger mix. Label every bowl and tray with the batch number, mix start, pipe completion, and oven entry. That record lets you match the 30 to 60 minute rest to each tray instead of treating the whole order as one resting block.

Run the same piping and loading routine for each batch. Start the next batch only when its tray can follow the same rest and baking sequence. The scale pastry batches guide can help you turn that repeatable order into a worksheet for scheduled production. Your tray plan then follows the method you already know, even when the order count grows.

secciones.h2: Which pack feeds the line?
secciones.texto:
Choose format from the number of batches and the interval between production sessions. A 1L Tetrapak covers about 8 macaron batches. A 200g pouch covers 25 batches when each batch uses 8g of powder made up with 120 ml water. For a larger liquid reserve, the 10L bag-in-box replaces 330 egg whites.

Unopened liquid and powder keep at least 12 months at room temperature. Once opened, liquid keeps 3 to 4 days at 2 to 6 °C. Keep opened powder dry and closed until its best-before date. Match that handling window to your production calendar before opening a pack.

secciones.h2: How do you validate the larger run?
secciones.texto:
Validate a new order size with a run you can review batch by batch. Five batches make about 200 filled macarons and use 600g of liquid aquafaba, or 40g of powder made up with 600 ml water. Keep the formula, rest, oven setting, and maturation time aligned with the recorded method.

Mark each tray by batch, then review the logs for whipping, macaronage, piping, resting, baking and maturation. Compare the complete run with the small-batch standard you already use. If a point changes, repeat the documented unit before moving to the next production volume.

faq.question: How much aquafaba do I need when I have an order for 400 macarons?
faq.answer: Plan 10 batches and 1.2kg of liquid aquafaba for about 400 filled macarons. If you use powder, use 80g made up with 1.2L water.

faq.question: Can I use powder when I scale my macaron production?
faq.answer: Yes. For one batch of about 40 filled macarons, make up 8g of powder with 120 ml water. Keep that batch unit the same as you build the order quantity.

faq.question: How long should I rest shells when I am working across several trays?
faq.answer: Rest each tray for 30 to 60 minutes. Record when piping finishes for each tray so its rest is tracked separately from the rest of the order.

faq.question: What should I check if I increase my aquafaba macaron batch size?
faq.answer: Check whipping, macaronage, piping, resting, baking and maturation in the same order as your usual batch. Bake at 130 °C for 16 to 18 minutes, then allow 24 hours for maturation after filling.

faq.question: Which pack should I use if I need several macaron batches?
faq.answer: A 1L Tetrapak covers about 8 batches, while a 200g pouch covers 25 batches. A 10L bag-in-box replaces 330 egg whites when you need a larger liquid format.

faq.question: How do I store liquid aquafaba after I open it for production?
faq.answer: Keep opened liquid aquafaba at 2 to 6 °C and use it within 3 to 4 days. Keep opened powder dry and closed until its best-before date.

end.cierre: Write the filled macaron count on your production sheet, select the matching batch row, and schedule each tray through the same rest and bake sequence. If you need a format for an upcoming order, use the calculator first, then send an enquiry with the batch count and pack format you are considering.

intro.title: Replace Egg Whites in Pastry Production
intro.description: Replace egg whites in a pastry production schedule with a 30g aquafaba conversion, recipe card edits, opened-pack planning, and first-week production checks.
intro.h1: How to replace egg whites in pastry production
intro.texto:
You are weighing meringue mix before the morning bake. Every egg white becomes 30g of aquafaba on the card, and you switch one recipe at a time.

We start with a recipe that already has a clear egg-white weight, then place its aquafaba batch into your usual prep sequence. Update the card before you make the next batch. Plan the opened liquid around the next 3 to 4 days, then record what happens at the bench. For a direct reference, 150g of aquafaba replaces 5 egg whites in a meringue batch with 150g of sugar, making about 30 meringues. You get a repeatable conversion rule, an opening-date routine, and a short check process before another card changes.

secciones.h2: Which recipes do you switch first?
secciones.texto:
Pick a product you make regularly and can inspect at more than one point in the process. Meringue gives a simple first card: 150g of aquafaba, 150g of sugar, and about 30 meringues. Chocolate mousse uses 120g for about 6 portions. Macarons also use 120g, for about 40 filled macarons.

Start with one of those production lines, not all of them. Keep the existing recipe card beside the rewritten version for the first run. This lets you review the specific mixing, folding, piping, or baking notes that matter to that item before you put another recipe into the schedule.

secciones.h2: How do you rewrite the recipe cards?
secciones.texto:
Keep the conversion on the weigh-up line, not in a separate note. Where the card lists egg whites by count, write the aquafaba weight beside the replacement ingredient. A card for 5 egg whites can state 150g of aquafaba, which gives the person on prep one clear quantity to scale.

Add fields for the opening date, the recipe version, and the bench notes from the first production run. If you use powder, write a separate preparation line: 2g of powder made up with 30 ml of water makes 32g of aquafaba and replaces one egg white. Make up only what the batch needs.

secciones.h2: How do you plan the opened packs across the week?
secciones.texto:
Give opened liquid its own place on the weekly prep list. Keep it at 2 to 6 °C, mark the opening date, and schedule it across the following 3 to 4 days. The table shows three documented recipe batches placed within three days of opening a liquid pack.

DayRecipeAquafaba
MondayMeringue150g
TuesdayChocolate mousse120g
WednesdayMacarons120g

Build the actual sequence from your order list and your pack format. If a later batch is not scheduled inside that storage window, keep an unopened liquid pack closed or make up the powder only when that batch is due.

secciones.h2: How do you check the first week?
secciones.texto:
Treat the first week as a production check, not a full rewrite of the pastry section. Record the recipe name, the aquafaba weight, the opening date, and what you see during mixing, piping, setting, or baking. Keep those notes with the card rather than relying on memory at the next prep.

Compare each finished batch with the standard you use for that product. If the card needs a clearer instruction, change that one line before the next scheduled batch. Once the revised card is clear at the bench, move to the next recipe and repeat the same check.

faq.question: How do I replace egg whites with aquafaba on my pastry card?
faq.answer: Write 30g of liquid aquafaba for each egg white on the card. Keep the conversion in grams so the weigh-up is clear at the bench.

faq.question: Which recipe should I switch first in my pastry production?
faq.answer: Choose one regular item with an existing card that gives a clear egg-white quantity. Meringue is one documented option: 150g of aquafaba with 150g of sugar makes about 30 meringues.

faq.question: How do I schedule an opened liquid pack if I only prep twice a week?
faq.answer: Open it for a planned batch, mark the date, and keep it at 2 to 6 °C. Opened liquid keeps for 3 to 4 days, so place another suitable batch inside that period or leave the next pack unopened.

faq.question: Can I make up only the aquafaba powder that I need?
faq.answer: Yes. Make up only what the batch needs: 2g of powder with 30 ml of water makes 32g of aquafaba and replaces one egg white.

faq.question: How much aquafaba do I use when I make meringue, mousse, or macarons?
faq.answer: Use 150g for the documented meringue batch, 120g for chocolate mousse, and 120g for macarons. Those amounts correspond to 5 egg whites for meringue and 4 egg whites for the mousse and macarons.

faq.question: What should I check when I make my first aquafaba batch?
faq.answer: Record the recipe version, aquafaba weight, opening date, and the handling notes that matter to the item. Review the finished batch against your usual product standard before changing the next card.

end.cierre: Open one card that is due in the next prep cycle. Replace its egg-white line with the 30g rule, date the liquid pack when you open it, and enter the first batch on a simple check sheet. Once that card reads clearly at the bench, schedule the next recipe rather than revising the whole section at once.

intro.title: Aquafaba powder bakery preparation and use
intro.description: Learn how to make up aquafaba powder, add it to bakery methods, store opened pouches, and choose a pouch that matches your daily bakery production schedule.
intro.h1: How do I prepare aquafaba powder for a bakery?
intro.texto: At the bench, before a tray of meringues or a fat-rich batter goes on the mixer, make aquafaba powder up with water. For each egg white your formula replaces, use 2g of powder with 30 ml of water, then add the made-up aquafaba, never dry powder, to the mix. That blend makes 32g of aquafaba, the same working weight as liquid aquafaba. When you replace whole eggs, begin by reducing the recipe's other liquids by 5 to 10%. The water used to make up the powder stays as given, so it is not part of that adjustment. For batters built around whipped egg whites, chill the made-up aquafaba before whipping. For fat-rich formulas, plan where it meets sugar and fat before you start the batch. That keeps the first conversion clear when you move from formula weights to your bakery method.

secciones.h2: How do you make up powder for a bake?
secciones.texto:
Set out a clean vessel of water before you scale the powder. For one egg-white replacement, 2g of powder and 30 ml of water make 32g of aquafaba. For a whole-egg replacement, use 3g of powder with 45 ml of water.

Mix the powder into the measured water before it reaches the formula, then weigh or portion that aquafaba into the batch. Do not scatter dry powder into flour, sugar, or a mixer bowl. Make up only the amount required for the bake, which keeps the recipe's water balance clear at the point of mixing.

secciones.h2: Where does made-up powder go in the method?
secciones.texto:
Follow the role that egg played in the original formula. In a fat-rich batter, mix the made-up aquafaba with the sugar before it meets the fat. This puts the ingredient into the method without treating the powder as a dry ingredient.

A formula built on whipped egg whites needs a different step. Chill the made-up aquafaba to 4 to 6 °C, whip it, then fold it into the batter. If you are converting whole eggs, reduce other recipe liquids by 5 to 10% as a starting point. Keep the make-up water unchanged when you make that adjustment.

secciones.h2: How do you store opened pouches?
secciones.texto:
Close the pouch as soon as you have scaled the powder and keep it dry. Opened powder that stays dry and closed keeps until the best-before date on the pouch. Read that date as the storage limit for the open pouch, rather than setting a separate day count.

Build the check into pre-batch preparation. Look at the best-before date before you scale the day's requirement and keep the pouch closed between uses. Unopened liquid and powder keep at least 12 months at room temperature, so an unopened pouch can stay in normal dry-store planning until you need it.

secciones.h2: Which pouch suits your production?
secciones.texto:
Match pouch size to the number of egg-white replacements on your production plan. A 30g pouch covers 15 egg whites, while a 200g pouch covers 100. The 3kg pouch covers 1,500 egg whites, so it calls for a production plan that accounts for its larger make-up volume.

A full 3kg pouch takes 45L of water and makes 48kg of aquafaba. That volume changes how you schedule vessels, scales, and batch size. For lower or irregular use, choose a format by the stated egg-white count. For repeated larger batches, compare that count with the quantities you plan to make up.

faq.question: Can I add aquafaba powder dry to my bakery mix?
faq.answer: No. Make it up with water before it goes into the formula. For one egg white, use 2g of powder with 30 ml of water.

faq.question: How do I replace a whole egg with aquafaba powder?
faq.answer: Use 3g of powder with 45 ml of water for each whole egg replacement. Start by reducing the recipe's other liquids by 5 to 10%, but do not reduce the water used to make up the powder.

faq.question: Where do I add made-up aquafaba in a fat-rich batter?
faq.answer: Mix the made-up aquafaba with the sugar before it meets the fat. This follows the method used for fat-rich batters rather than adding dry powder with the other dry ingredients.

faq.question: How do I use made-up aquafaba in a recipe with whipped egg whites?
faq.answer: Chill the made-up aquafaba to 4 to 6 °C before whipping it. Fold it into the batter after whipping, following the role of the egg whites in the original method.

faq.question: How long can I keep an opened aquafaba powder pouch?
faq.answer: An opened pouch keeps until its best-before date when it stays dry and closed. Check the printed date before you scale powder for the next batch.

faq.question: Which aquafaba powder pouch should I choose for my bakery?
faq.answer: Use the egg-white count on each pouch to match your planned output. The 30g pouch covers 15 egg whites, the 200g pouch covers 100, and the 3kg pouch covers 1,500.

end.cierre: Put the powder and water weights on the production sheet for the next formula you convert. Make up only the amount for that batch, check the pouch best-before before prep, and select the format against your planned egg-white replacements. If you need help matching a pouch to your output, send an enquiry.

intro.title: Scaling pastry recipes: egg whites, grams and pouches
intro.description: Scale pastry recipes from egg whites or grams with clear aquafaba conversions, pouch planning, and batch records for repeatable production work at scale.
intro.h1: How do you scale pastry recipes with egg whites for production?
intro.texto: The mixer is running, trays are waiting, and the bench formula still says 10 egg whites. To scale pastry recipes with egg whites for production, convert each white to 30g of liquid VERY AQUAFABA, then keep the conversion in grams through the batch. For a formula written with 10 egg whites, use 300g of liquid. If you work from powder, use 20g with 300 ml of water for the same conversion. We use a clear production order: set the batch size, choose the pouch that covers it, then record the method and yield details that matter on your line. This gives you a practical route from a bench formula to a production sheet for meringue, mousse, and macarons.

secciones.h2: How do you scale a recipe written in egg whites?
secciones.texto:
Start with the egg-white quantity in the original formula and set the batch factor before you weigh anything. Each egg white converts to 30g of liquid VERY AQUAFABA. A meringue formula using 5 egg whites therefore uses 150g, while mousse and macaron formulas can each use 120g for 4 egg whites.

Keep the remaining ingredients in their original weight-based units. Do not treat whole eggs as egg whites: one whole egg is 45g. We keep the egg-white conversion on the batch sheet, so there is one clear ingredient weight to follow. Use the egg white converter to check the starting weight before you release the scaled formula.

secciones.h2: How do you scale one written in grams?
secciones.texto:
Use the gram weight in the formula as the production control point. That avoids converting back to egg counts after the bench recipe has been approved. Match the required liquid weight to VERY AQUAFABA, or make up the listed powder with water. The working rule is that 2g of powder with 30 ml of water makes 32g of aquafaba and replaces one egg white. The table sets out the fixed conversions for common batch sizes. Put the chosen format beside the ingredient weight on the production sheet. Use the powder calculator when you need to check a different egg-white count.
Egg whitesLiquid aquafabaPowderWaterPouch that covers the batch

secciones.h2: How do you match the batch to a pouch?
secciones.texto:
Choose the pouch after you have set the full egg-white equivalent for the run, not from the weight of a single component. A 30g powder pouch replaces 15 egg whites. A 200g pouch replaces 100, and a 3kg pouch replaces 1,500.

For a batch specified as 100 egg whites, the 200g pouch is the stated match when made up with 3L of water. Keep a format note beside the formula, especially when several pastry items draw from the same pre-batch. We use the 200g pouch for the common table entries beyond 10 egg whites, while the 3kg pouch suits a much larger planned requirement.

secciones.h2: What do you record when the batch grows?
secciones.texto:
A larger batch needs more than a revised ingredient line. Record the original formula, the target batch, every ingredient in grams, and whether the aquafaba was liquid or powder made up with water. Add the pouch format, the mixing method, the order of additions, the equipment used, and the yield you actually portioned.

Note any change you make before the next run, rather than relying on a memory at the bench. We keep those details together with the formula so a future pre-batch starts from the same written method. For work on shells or foam, the guides scale macarons for production and meringue in larger batches provide related process checks.

faq.question: How do I convert egg whites to aquafaba for a larger pastry batch?
faq.answer: Use 30g of liquid VERY AQUAFABA for each egg white listed in the formula. Set the full formula batch first, then keep that aquafaba weight and the remaining ingredients in grams.

faq.question: How do I make up powder for an egg-white pastry formula?
faq.answer: Use 2g of powder with 30 ml of water for each egg white you need to replace. This makes 32g of aquafaba per egg-white replacement.

faq.question: If I need 100 egg whites, which pouch should I plan?
faq.answer: A 200g pouch covers 100 egg whites. For this conversion, make the powder up with 3L of water to produce 3kg of aquafaba.

faq.question: Can I use this conversion in macarons, meringue, and mousse?
faq.answer: The stated recipe equivalents are 120g for macarons and mousse, each listed as 4 egg whites. The meringue recipe lists 150g, stated as 5 egg whites.

faq.question: What do I need to record when I increase a pastry batch?
faq.answer: Record the formula version, target batch, ingredient weights, pouch format, water used for powder, mixing method, equipment, and portioned yield. Keep changes to the method with the same production sheet.

faq.question: How do I plan powder when several pastry items share one pre-batch?
faq.answer: Add the egg-white equivalents required by the planned formulas, then choose the format based on that total. Record the powder and water made up, plus the pouch selected, on the same production sheet.

end.cierre: Start with one live production formula. Write its egg-white requirement, select liquid or powder, and put the corresponding gram weight and pouch format on the batch sheet. Check a conversion with the egg white converter or powder calculator, then send an enquiry if you need to discuss the format for your planned production.

intro.title: Egg-free pastry bakery chain rollout
intro.description: Plan an egg-free pastry bakery chain rollout: choose a first product, standardize the recipe, manage supply and describe aquafaba clearly to customers.
intro.h1: How do I roll out egg-free pastries across a bakery chain?
intro.texto: At the bench, a formula that works in one shop still has to survive production cards, ordering and customer questions in every other shop. Start by trialing one pastry in one shop, write its card with aquafaba in grams, then roll it out after it meets your checks. For an egg-free pastry bakery chain rollout, choose a product with a clear egg-white role, lock the gram weight, and give every shop the same handling instruction. 30g of liquid VERY AQUAFABA replaces one egg white. That rule gives the card a unit your bakers can weigh, rather than a variable egg count. We recommend beginning with one repeatable line, then moving through the formula, supply route and counter wording in that order. This keeps the rollout focused on the work a shop has to perform, from pre-batch through display.

secciones.h2: Which products do you roll out first?
secciones.texto:
Begin where egg white has a defined job in the current method and where the product is made often enough for the trial to be observed in normal production. Do not change several pastries at once. A single formula lets you see whether the card, method and finished item are clear to the baker making it.

Pick one shop that can run the product through its usual prep, bake and display routine. Record the aquafaba in grams, the method stage where it enters and the sign-off points you already use. If the role is a whole egg or yolk rather than egg white, the conversion changes: one whole egg is 45g, while one egg yolk is 15g of aquafaba plus 10g of oil.

secciones.h2: How do you keep the recipe the same in every shop?
secciones.texto:
Your recipe card has to remove judgment calls at the bench. Name the format, the weight in grams, the stage of the method and the handling instruction. Write liquid VERY AQUAFABA and 30g for each egg white being replaced, rather than asking bakers to convert eggs during prep.

Keep one approved master card and issue the same version to every shop. If you use powder, state the make-up method on that card: 2g of powder with 30 ml of water makes 32g of aquafaba and replaces one egg white. Keep the trial record with the card, so a change to an ingredient or method can be reviewed before it reaches other shops.

secciones.h2: How do you supply each shop?
secciones.texto:
Set each shop's order pattern after the single-shop trial, using the quantities on its approved card and its own production rhythm. For liquid format, opened stock keeps 3 to 4 days at 2 to 6 °C. Make that storage window part of the shop instruction before you decide order frequency.

Unopened liquid and powder keep at least 12 months at room temperature. Opened powder, kept dry and closed, keeps until its best-before date. We serve every country through distributors. For a chain operating in more than one country, tell us the countries and formats needed when you contact us.

secciones.h2: How do you describe the products to customers?
secciones.texto:
Counter wording should say what has actually been checked. You can describe VERY AQUAFABA itself as plant-based and egg-free. Do not describe the finished pastry as vegan until every ingredient in that recipe has been checked.

Keep allergen language just as narrow. VERY AQUAFABA contains no egg, dairy, gluten or soy. Chickpea is not one of the 14 allergens covered by EU mandatory allergen labelling, but chickpea and other legume allergies can exist. Check every ingredient in the pastry before making an allergen statement, and do not use a broad allergen-free claim for the pastry.

faq.question: How do I replace egg whites in my chain pastry card?
faq.answer: Use 30g of liquid VERY AQUAFABA for one egg white. Put the gram weight and the point where it enters the method on the approved recipe card.

faq.question: Which egg-free pastry should I trial first across my shops?
faq.answer: Start with one product where egg white has a clearly defined role in the existing formula. Run it in one shop first, using its usual prep, bake and display routine.

faq.question: How do I store liquid aquafaba after opening in each shop?
faq.answer: Opened liquid keeps 3 to 4 days at 2 to 6 °C. Include that handling window on the shop instruction before setting an order pattern.

faq.question: Can I use powder instead of liquid for my bakery chain?
faq.answer: Yes, 2g of powder made up with 30 ml of water makes 32g of aquafaba and replaces one egg white. Keep opened powder dry and closed, and it keeps until its best-before date.

faq.question: Can I call my pastry vegan when I use aquafaba?
faq.answer: You can describe VERY AQUAFABA as plant-based and egg-free. Only describe the finished pastry as vegan after checking every ingredient in that recipe.

faq.question: How do I arrange aquafaba supply for shops in different countries?
faq.answer: We serve every country through distributors. Send an enquiry with the countries, formats and products involved, and we reply within two working days. The route then moves through exploration, specification, a trial in your product, and quote and supply after a validated trial.

end.cierre: Choose one product and one shop. Put the aquafaba weight and handling notes on a trial card, then run it through your usual checks. When the formula is ready to discuss, send the product, format and countries involved in an enquiry.
