intro.title: Aquafaba central kitchen quantity planning
intro.description: Plan aquafaba quantities for multi-site kitchens: total recipe demand, choose a format, manage opened packs across shifts, and set a clear weekly order.
intro.h1: How do I plan aquafaba quantities for a central kitchen?
intro.texto:
Total the egg whites in the week’s recipes and convert at 30g each. A 10L bag-in-box replaces 330 egg whites, so you can turn recipe sheets from several sites into one central requirement.

At the start of a production week, your bench plan may combine dessert prep, sauces and dispatch for different kitchens. Count each recipe batch before choosing a format or opening stock. For example, 20 mousse batches need 2.4kg of aquafaba and 10 mayonnaise batches need 600g. That weekly plan comes to 3kg, or 100 egg whites’ worth. Use the same method for every item on the production board, then separate what you need to open this week from unopened stock for later production.

secciones.h2: How do you total a week of production?
secciones.texto:
Start with every recipe scheduled for central production, then add the aquafaba requirement for each batch. A chocolate mousse batch uses 120g, which is equal to 4 egg whites. A mayonnaise batch uses 60g. Keep the count in one weekly worksheet so dessert, cold prep and site orders are visible together.

The worked plan of 20 mousse batches and 10 mayonnaise batches requires 3kg in total. This gives you a practical check before prep begins. If a site changes its order, update the relevant batch line and review the central total before allocating stock.

secciones.h2: Which format fits a central kitchen?
secciones.texto:
Choose the format around the quantity you will use, the storage space available and how often your production schedule opens a pack. A 10L bag-in-box replaces 330 egg whites and suits a kitchen that draws liquid aquafaba steadily across planned production.

For dry storage and larger converted egg-white requirements, a 3kg powder pouch replaces 1,500 egg whites. A 1L Tetrapak replaces 33 egg whites when a smaller liquid volume matches the plan. Match the format to the weekly worksheet, rather than treating every site order as a separate purchase.

secciones.h2: How do you plan opened packs across shifts?
secciones.texto:
Assign opened liquid aquafaba to named production days before the first pack is opened. Keep opened liquid at 2 to 6 °C and use it within 3 to 4 days. This makes it easier to place mousse, mayonnaise and other planned prep within the same opening window.

Record the opening day on the production sheet and keep the next shift’s requirement visible. If the planned work does not use a full liquid pack in that period, adjust the format or opening schedule for the next week. Opened powder can stay until its best-before date when kept dry and closed.

secciones.h2: How do you order for the week?

Build the order from the final weekly total, then check how much unopened stock is already on hand. Keep the figures in the same unit used on your recipe sheets, then convert that total into the format you intend to receive and store.

Unopened liquid and powder keep for at least 12 months at room temperature. That lets you separate the quantity needed for this week’s prep from stock intended for later production. Review the order after site changes are confirmed, especially when mousse and mayonnaise batches move between production days.

faq.question: How do I convert my egg-white total into aquafaba?

faq.question: How do I plan aquafaba for mousse and mayonnaise in the same week?

faq.question: Can I keep opened aquafaba powder for later production?

faq.question: How do I order aquafaba for several sites from one kitchen?

intro.title: Egg-free desserts for catering menu cycles
intro.description: Plan egg-free desserts across a catering menu cycle, from identifying egg-led recipes and setting quantities to storage dates and clear menu wording for diners.
intro.h1: How do you plan egg-free desserts across a catering menu cycle?
intro.texto: As you close the next menu cycle, plan egg-free desserts by mapping every recipe where egg creates structure, foam or a finish. Then set the batch size, format and service date before the production sheet goes out. For opened liquid, build production around 3 to 4 days at 2 to 6 °C. That rule keeps the pastry list tied to the stock routine, rather than adding an egg-free dessert as a late exception. We start with the dishes you already serve, such as mousse or meringue, and decide which ones need an egg-free version in the rotation. You can then match confirmed covers to a tested batch, keep opened formats visible in the chiller or dry store, and describe the finished dessert without making a claim the full recipe does not support.

secciones.h2: Which desserts in the cycle use egg?
secciones.texto:
Begin at the pastry section of the existing rota. Mark each dessert where egg provides foam, structure, coating or a visible finish. This stops you treating every recipe as the same swap. Mousse and meringue give you practical places to set a repeatable egg-free method.

A chocolate mousse batch uses 120g of aquafaba, 100g of sugar and 180g of chocolate for about 6 portions. It needs at least 2 hours to set, and the finished mousse keeps 3 days in the fridge. A meringue batch uses 150g of aquafaba and 150g of sugar for about 30 meringues, then bakes at 90 °C for 1.5 to 2 hours. Put these production limits beside the service day.

secciones.h2: How do you plan the quantities across the cycle?
secciones.texto:
Plan from confirmed covers and the dessert’s role in the cycle. A plated mousse, a grab-and-go meringue and a buffet item do not draw stock in the same pattern. Keep the recipe yield, service date and any pre-batch day together on one production sheet, then choose the format that matches the frequency of use.

For liquid, a 1L Tetrapak replaces 33 egg whites and a 10L bag-in-box replaces 330. Powder formats are 30g for 15 egg whites, 200g for 100 egg whites and 3kg for 1,500 egg whites. Use the chocolate mousse and meringue yields as your batch reference. This lets you check the cycle before you open a format.

secciones.h2: How do you keep opened stock within its dates?
secciones.texto:
Keep unopened and opened stock on separate checks. Unopened liquid and powder keep at least 12 months at room temperature. Once opened, liquid needs a dated label and chiller position because it keeps 3 to 4 days at 2 to 6 °C.

Match liquid to runs that will use it inside that window. If the cycle has longer gaps between pastry sessions, opened powder can remain in use until its best-before date when it stays dry and closed. Record the opening date, format and planned dessert against the batch sheet. Review that record before adding a late function or changing the dessert rotation.

secciones.h2: How do you describe the desserts on the menu?
secciones.texto:
Name the dessert for what the full recipe contains, not for one component. “Egg-free chocolate mousse” can be clear when every ingredient in the served recipe has been checked. “Vegan” needs the same full-recipe check, including chocolate, toppings, biscuits, sauces and any garnish.

Do not use “allergen-free” for these desserts. VERY AQUAFABA contains no egg, dairy, gluten or soy, but chickpea and other legume allergies can exist. Anyone with a known chickpea allergy should still avoid it. Keep the menu name straightforward, then make sure the recipe sheet and service information match it.

faq.question: How do I find the desserts in my cycle that need an egg-free option?
faq.answer: Review the complete dessert rota and flag recipes where egg creates the foam, structure, coating or finish. Start with the items repeated across the cycle, then decide whether to convert them or schedule an egg-free alternative.

faq.question: How do I plan egg-free chocolate mousse quantities for my contract catering covers?
faq.answer: Use the batch reference of 120g of aquafaba, 100g of sugar and 180g of chocolate for about 6 portions. Keep the confirmed service count and the minimum 2-hour setting time on the same production sheet.

faq.question: How do I keep opened liquid aquafaba within its date?
faq.answer: Date the opened pack and keep it at 2 to 6 °C. Opened liquid keeps 3 to 4 days, so allocate it to desserts already scheduled inside that period.

faq.question: Can I use powder when my dessert dates are spread across the cycle?
faq.answer: Yes, opened powder keeps until its best-before date when it stays dry and closed. It can suit cycles with gaps between pastry sessions, while liquid can suit tightly scheduled production runs.

faq.question: Can I call my egg-free dessert vegan or allergen-free?
faq.answer: You can use “vegan” only after checking every ingredient in the finished recipe. Do not call the dessert “allergen-free”, because chickpea and other legume allergies can exist even though chickpea is not one of the 14 allergens covered by EU mandatory allergen labelling.

faq.question: How do I set up egg-free dessert batches for a central kitchen and events?
faq.answer: Keep the recipe yield, service date, setting or baking time, format and opening date together on the production sheet. This gives each kitchen or event service the same reference before the dessert is prepared.

Use the pastry section planner before you release the production sheets.

intro.title: Chocolate mousse for 300 people: catering guide

Keep this run built around one defined batch, then repeat the same melting, whipping, folding and chilling sequence. You can also decide before prep whether liquid aquafaba or powder fits the way your central kitchen receives, stores and stages ingredients.

secciones.h2: How much do you need for 300 portions?

For a plated or buffet service, build the whole run from the same six-portion batch. Each batch uses 120g of aquafaba, 100g of sugar and 180g of chocolate. The production totals below keep the recipe unchanged as the guest count rises.

secciones.h2: How do you organize the production run?

When 300 desserts are due from a central kitchen, stage ingredients in repeatable batch groups and keep the method fixed for every mix. Write the sequence on the production sheet, including the temperature checks and the chilling handoff.

intro.title: Standardize recipes for delivery kitchens

intro.h1: How do you standardize aquafaba mousse across delivery kitchens?
intro.texto: At the pass, you need each delivery kitchen to make mousse from the same instructions, weighed ingredients, and temperature checks. Use one master card built around 120g of aquafaba, 100g of sugar, and 180g of chocolate for about 6 portions, then make that card the working standard in every kitchen without pausing for local reinterpretation during a busy prep window. The risk is not the recipe itself. It is a kitchen changing the order, folding chocolate while it is too warm, or storing an opened pack without the same handover notes. A shared card turns those choices into visible checks. This guide sets out the card, the production controls, the formats for different volumes, and the checks to use before mousse leaves each kitchen.

secciones.h2: How do you write one recipe card for every kitchen?

Put the full base batch at the top, not a ratio that each kitchen must interpret. The card should state 120g aquafaba, 100g sugar and 180g chocolate, with an output of about 6 portions. Name the bowl size only if it is identical across sites, otherwise describe the observable stage.

Put the method in production order: melt the chocolate at 45 to 50 °C, whip the aquafaba for 3 to 4 minutes, then fold only when the chocolate reaches 35 °C or lower. End with a minimum setting time of 2 hours. Leave one version-controlled file where each kitchen can access it, and remove older prints from prep stations.

secciones.h2: How do you keep the result the same?
secciones.texto:
Consistency starts before whipping. Issue the same aquafaba format for the card, use scales for the ingredient weights, and define the same chilled holding point after folding. Record the batch date, the chocolate temperature at folding, and the time it entered refrigeration.

Keep the release check practical. Compare each batch against the agreed portion yield and setting time, then hold any batch where a recorded step is missing. Do not solve a mismatch by altering the card at one site. Record the issue, follow the shared method on the next batch, and update the master card only when the change is agreed for every kitchen.

secciones.h2: How do you supply each kitchen?

Choose the format from each kitchen's throughput and storage routine, then send the same format whenever the master card requires it. A 1L Tetrapak replaces 33 egg whites, while a 10L bag-in-box replaces 330. Powder comes in 30g, 200g and 3kg pouches, replacing 15, 100 and 1,500 egg whites respectively.

Unopened liquid and powder keep for at least 12 months at room temperature. Once opened, liquid keeps for 3 to 4 days at 2 to 6 °C. Keep opened powder dry and closed until its best-before date. We serve every country through distributors, so group location needs into one ordering brief before you place an enquiry.

secciones.h2: How do you check a kitchen's mousse?
secciones.texto:
Make the same checks at the same point in the workflow. Confirm that the chocolate was folded at 35 °C or lower, that the mousse had at least 2 hours to set, and that portioning follows the card. Check the production record before dispatch, not after a customer report.

Use the finished holding limit on the card as well. Finished mousse keeps 3 days in the fridge, so label each batch with its production date and keep handovers clear between shifts. For a new kitchen, run the base recipe first, compare its record with the master card, and correct the process rather than changing quantities from memory.

faq.question: How do I scale the mousse card for several delivery kitchens?

intro.title: Switch egg to aquafaba production: specs and trials
intro.description: Plan an egg-to-aquafaba production switch with formula ratios, label checks, product trials and a controlled switchover for foods already on sale today.
intro.h1: How do I switch egg to aquafaba production?
intro.texto: You can switch egg to aquafaba production by resetting formula weights, reviewing the finished-food label, and approving a trial against your own release criteria. On the production floor, the change begins when a recipe already on sale moves from cracked egg or liquid egg to a measured aquafaba input. For an egg-white replacement, start with 30g of liquid aquafaba for each egg white. Whole egg and yolk replacements need their own formula review, because water and fat move differently through the batch. We recommend working through specification first, then testing the actual product and its process before you alter purchasing, packaging, or release records. That sequence gives you a clear way to compare the existing recipe with the proposed one, document the decision points, and plan the change with the documents and supply route available for professional projects.

secciones.h2: What changes in the specification?
secciones.texto:
Start with the ingredient role, not the old egg count. Use 30g of liquid aquafaba for each egg white, 45g for each whole egg, and 15g of aquafaba plus 10g of oil for each egg yolk. Record those changes in grams within the proposed formula.

Aquafaba is 90 to 95% water, while a whole egg is about 75% water. When replacing whole eggs, begin by reducing the other liquids in the recipe by 5 to 10%. Use balance the water in a formula before judging the finished product. You can also compare aquafaba with egg white fairly by matching the functional role and gram weight rather than comparing ingredients by volume.

secciones.h2: What do you check on the label?
secciones.texto:
Review the finished-food label when the formula changes. VERY AQUAFABA lists water and chickpeas as its ingredients, and it contains no egg, dairy, gluten, or soy. Those points describe the aquafaba ingredient, not every ingredient in the food you make.

Check your own label rules and every other ingredient before deciding how to describe the finished product. Chickpea is not one of the 14 allergens covered by EU mandatory allergen labelling, but chickpea and other legume allergies can exist. Anyone with a known chickpea or legume allergy should still avoid it. Review what the technical sheet covers before requesting the product information needed for your records.

intro.title: Aquafaba definition: professional glossary
intro.description: Learn the aquafaba definition and the ingredient, format, kitchen, bar and documentation terms professionals use when specifying, handling and ordering it.
intro.h1: What is aquafaba?
intro.texto: At the pass or bar station, you need a precise name on the prep sheet before service starts. Aquafaba is the cooking water of chickpeas, filtered, refined and standardized so it performs consistently from batch to batch. In professional use, it can foam for cocktails, meringue, mousse and macarons. It can also emulsify mayonnaise and bind baking mixtures. The working conversion is 30g of liquid VERY AQUAFABA for one egg white. This glossary separates ingredient names, pack formats, preparation methods and buying documents. You can match each term to a recipe, production note or purchasing request.

secciones.h2: Ingredient and format terms
secciones.texto:
• Aquafaba. Filtered, refined and standardized chickpea cooking water that foams, emulsifies and binds.
  • Chickpea water. The cooking liquid from chickpeas. In this glossary, it names the liquid before filtering, refining and standardization are stated.
  • VERY AQUAFABA powder. A dry format. 2g mixed with 30 ml of water makes 32g of aquafaba, the equivalent of one egg white.
  • Making up. Mixing powder with its measured water before use.
  • Tetrapak. A 1L liquid format containing 33 egg-white equivalents.
  • Bag-in-box. A 10L liquid format containing 330 egg-white equivalents.
  • IBC. A 1T liquid format containing 33,000 egg-white equivalents.

secciones.h2: Kitchen and bar techniques
secciones.texto:
• Dry shake. Shaking without ice for 10 to 15 seconds. It starts building the foam before ice is added.
  • Wet shake. Shaking with ice for 10 to 15 seconds after the dry shake.
  • Jigger. The measuring tool used to pour 20 ml of aquafaba per cocktail.
  • Pre-batch. Combining spirit, citrus and syrup before service, without the aquafaba.
  • Soft peaks. Foam peaks that bend over when lifted.
  • Stiff peaks. Foam peaks that hold upright when lifted.
  • Macaronage. The controlled folding stage that turns whipped macaron mixture into a pipeable batter.
  • Emulsion. A mixture where fine droplets of one liquid are dispersed through another.

secciones.h2: Buying and documentation terms
secciones.texto:
• Technical sheet, or TDS. The document that describes the product.
  • Certificate of analysis, or COA. A document belonging to one production batch, rather than to every batch generally.
  • Production batch. The specific lot connected to a COA.
  • Best-before date. The date printed on a powder pouch for storage while it remains dry and closed.
  • Unopened storage. Liquid and powder keep for at least 12 months at room temperature.
  • Opened liquid storage. Liquid keeps for 3 to 4 days at 2 to 6 °C after opening.

secciones.h2: How do you use these terms with us?
secciones.texto:
• Ready-made liquid. VERY AQUAFABA in liquid form, available in 1L Tetrapak, 10L bag-in-box and 1T IBC formats.
  • Powder pouch. Powder is available in 30g, 200g and 3kg pouches, representing 15, 100 and 1,500 egg-white equivalents.
  • Egg conversion. Use 45g of liquid VERY AQUAFABA for one whole egg. For one egg yolk, use 15g of aquafaba plus 10g of oil.
  • Documentation request. Ask for the TDS when you need the product description and the COA when you need the record for a specific production batch.

faq.question: What do I mean when I say aquafaba?
faq.answer: Aquafaba means chickpea cooking water used as a functional ingredient. VERY AQUAFABA is filtered, refined and standardized so it can be specified for foaming, emulsifying and binding work.

faq.question: Can I call any chickpea water aquafaba?
faq.answer: You can use chickpea water as a general description of the cooking liquid. When you need a repeatable ingredient specification, state whether it is filtered, refined and standardized aquafaba.

faq.question: How do I make up aquafaba powder?
faq.answer: Mix 2g of powder with 30 ml of water before using it. That makes 32g of aquafaba, which replaces one egg white.

faq.question: How do I use aquafaba in a cocktail?
faq.answer: Measure 20 ml with a jigger for each drink. Dry shake without ice for 10 to 15 seconds, then wet shake with ice for 10 to 15 seconds.

faq.question: What documents do I ask for when I buy aquafaba?
faq.answer: Ask for the TDS when you need a product description. Ask for the COA when you need documentation for a specific production batch, as it belongs to that batch.
